---
description: Find and queue backlink prospects for a keyword or competitor
---
Call the seo-manager MCP tool `get_instructions` with workflow `backlinks` and follow the returned markdown exactly. Target: $ARGUMENTS

---
description: Build the oldest approved SEO tool suggestion as a PR (tools only)
---
Call the seo-manager MCP tool `get_instructions` with workflow `build-tool` and follow the returned markdown exactly (it is the current playbook; also read `.dispatchseo/conventions.md` for this repo's site facts). Tools ONLY - type="tool". If no approved tool suggestions exist, exit without changes.

---
description: Build the oldest approved SEO guide suggestion as a PR (guides only)
---
Call the seo-manager MCP tool `get_instructions` with workflow `build-guide` and follow the returned markdown exactly (it is the current playbook; also read `.dispatchseo/conventions.md` for this repo's site facts). Guides ONLY - type="guide". If no approved guide suggestions exist, exit without changes.

---
description: Summarize rankings, GSC trends, and next SEO actions
---
Call the seo-manager MCP tool `get_instructions` with workflow `report` and follow the returned markdown exactly.

---
description: Research SEO keywords from product knowledge, track winners, queue suggestions
---
Call the seo-manager MCP tool `get_instructions` with workflow `research` and follow the returned markdown exactly (it is the current playbook; also read `.dispatchseo/conventions.md` for this repo's site facts). Topic scope (optional): $ARGUMENTS

---
description: One-time setup - write the site facts file and personalize the backlink playbook
---
Call the seo-manager MCP tool `get_instructions` with workflow `setup` and follow the returned markdown exactly (it writes/refreshes `.dispatchseo/conventions.md` from this repo's actual files, then personalizes the site profile via `set_site_profile`).

# Codex's twin of mcp-ci.json - the MCP servers the scheduled builders use
# when this project runs on Codex.
#
# Two files rather than one because the two agents genuinely disagree on
# format: Claude Code takes JSON with a `headers` map, Codex takes TOML and has
# no header option reachable from its config for the bearer case. Which one a
# run uses is decided at RUN time from the project's `agent` setting, so this
# file riding along in a Claude project costs nothing and is what makes
# switching agents on the dashboard take effect without touching the repo.
#
# The workflows copy this to $CODEX_HOME/config.toml before invoking Codex;
# CODEX_HOME is the only scoping Codex offers.

[mcp_servers.seo-manager]
url = "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/mcp"
# The NAME of an env var, not the token. Codex resolves it from the step's
# environment at call time, so the key never lands on the runner's disk - which
# is strictly better than the JSON twin, where ${SEO_MCP_API_KEY} is expanded
# into the file.
bearer_token_env_var = "SEO_MCP_API_KEY"
# What actually authorises a tool call. Without it every call comes back
# "user cancelled MCP tool call" - there is nobody on a scheduled runner to
# approve one - and no amount of sandbox widening changes that, because this is
# an approval and not a permission. Verified 2026-07-30 on codex-cli 0.146.0:
# with this line a call completes at sandbox=read-only with approvals=never.
default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"

# Codex ships with web search off. Claude Code has WebSearch built in, and the
# playbooks assume it exists - geo-scan outright REQUIRES real searches and
# forbids answering from memory. Without this line a Codex geo-scan either
# fabricates its answers or fails every week; with it the two agents hold the
# same contract. (Key verified against codex-rs config_toml.rs: ToolsToml.web_search.)
[tools]
web_search = true

# --- dataforseo ---
# Keep this section LAST and keep the marker line above exactly as written:
# getPipelinePack truncates the file there for projects with no DataForSEO
# account. See the comment beside that strip for why a truncate rather than a
# TOML round trip.
#
# The ${DATAFORSEO_*} tokens are NOT expanded by Codex - its TOML `env` map is
# literal values (mcp_types.rs), unlike the JSON twin where Claude expands
# ${VAR} itself, and `env_vars` cannot rename LOGIN -> USERNAME. The workflows'
# "Write Codex's MCP config" step substitutes real values for these tokens at
# run time, on the runner, before Codex ever reads the file. Keep the token
# spelling exactly as written or that substitution misses.
[mcp_servers.dataforseo]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "dataforseo-mcp-server@3.1.3"]
env = { DATAFORSEO_USERNAME = "${DATAFORSEO_LOGIN}", DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD = "${DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD}", ENABLED_MODULES = "SERP,DATAFORSEO_LABS,BACKLINKS" }
default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"

name: SEO auto-merge

# Hands-off publish gate for the SEO pipeline. Runs when checks report (plus
# an hourly backstop) and merges an open PR labeled `seo` ONLY when both are
# true:
#   1. It is auto-mergeable content:
#      - GUIDE PR: every changed file lives under this repo's publish dirs.
#        Those come from .dispatchseo/publish-paths on the default branch
#        (one path prefix per line, # comments allowed) - written at
#        install/setup time, owned by the repo, and NEVER shipped in the
#        pipeline pack, so a pack update cannot clobber the adaptation
#        (2026-07-23: an update overwrote an edited gate and a green guide
#        PR sat unmerged while the dashboard said it was live). Without the
#        file, the reference-stack defaults apply: src/content/blog/,
#        src/components/blog/, public/blog/covers/.
#      - TOOL PR (label `seo-tool`): carries the `tool-validated` label,
#        meaning seo-tool-validate built the PR, exercised the LIVE page in a
#        real browser, and proved the widget works.
#      Anything else (structural changes, unvalidated tools) waits for the owner.
#   2. Every automated check has PASSED - pnpm build, Vercel preview,
#      CodeRabbit, tool validation. Any pending check -> retry on the next
#      check event. Any failing check -> leave the PR for the owner. Zero checks ->
#      do NOT merge (no gate = not safe).
# This is the "green-checks gate" chosen deliberately over immediate merge, so
# nothing reaches the live, indexed site without passing every automated gate.

on:
  # Event-driven: sweep the moment any check reports, so a green guide PR
  # merges within a minute of its last check instead of waiting for the hour.
  # Both triggers are needed - CodeRabbit reports via the Checks API
  # (check_suite) while Vercel reports via commit statuses (status), and
  # Vercel's deploy is usually the check that finishes last.
  check_suite:
    types: [completed]
  status:
  # Backstop for anything the events miss (e.g. a check that never reports, or
  # GitHub dropping an event) and the pacing for the stalled-validation sweep
  # below, which polls rather than reacting to a payload.
  # Every 6h, not hourly: this job bills a full minute per run (see the cost
  # gate on the job), so an hourly sweep cost ~300 min/month of an installed
  # repo's GitHub Actions quota - 15% of the GitHub Free allowance - almost
  # always to discover there was nothing to merge. The merge path itself is
  # event-driven and unaffected: a green PR still merges within a minute of
  # its last check reporting. This only widens the worst case when an event is
  # genuinely dropped (a guide publishes up to 6h late) and the re-dispatch
  # window for a crashed tool validation, which is weekly work anyway.
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 */6 * * *" # 4x/day, offset off the top of the hour
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: seo-auto-merge
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # continue-on-error at JOB level: a failure still runs the failure() steps
    # and still reports to the dashboard rails, but the RUN concludes green so
    # GitHub never emails the repo owner "Run failed". The dashboard Home
    # banner / get_cron_health are the alerting surface for these runs.
    continue-on-error: true
    # COST GATE, at job level on purpose. GitHub bills every job that claims a
    # runner a minimum of one WHOLE minute, so a 10-second sweep that finds
    # nothing to do still costs a full minute. `status:` fires on EVERY commit
    # status event, and Vercel alone posts several per preview deploy (pending
    # while it builds, then success), so most of those minutes were spent
    # waking a runner to discover a check was still in progress. A job skipped
    # by an `if:` at this level never claims a runner and costs nothing -
    # which an early `exit 0` inside the job cannot do, because by then the
    # minute is already billed.
    #
    # Safe to skip: a status of `pending`, `failure` or `error` cannot make a
    # PR green, so there is never anything to merge on one. The stalled-
    # validation sweep further down polls open tool PRs by label instead of
    # reading this event payload, so it loses no signal either - the schedule
    # backstop below is what paces it. `check_suite`, `schedule` and
    # `workflow_dispatch` are deliberately unaffected.
    if: github.event_name != 'status' || github.event.state == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Bounded on purpose: this job holds a GLOBAL, non-cancelling concurrency
    # lock (group: seo-auto-merge above), so one wedged `gh` call would block ALL
    # merging on the repo for GitHub-s 360-minute default. It is also the only
    # job in the pack that had no bound at all.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      actions: write # re-run crashed tool validations (self-healing step below)
      checks: read # statusCheckRollup reads check runs (CodeRabbit et al.)
      statuses: read # ...and commit statuses (Vercel)
    steps:
      # Local-backend guard FIRST. On a self-host whose backend lives on the
      # owner's own machine (localhost/LAN), GitHub's runners can never reach
      # it - the install disables this workflow, but check events can fire it
      # in the gap between the install PR merging and that disable. Without
      # this guard that gap emails the owner a scary "run failed" for a
      # workflow that has nothing to do on their install anyway.
      - name: Local backend? Nothing for GitHub-hosted runs to do
        id: guard
        run: |
          case "{{BACKEND_URL}}" in
            http://localhost*|http://127.*|http://0.0.0.0*|http://10.*|http://192.168.*|http://172.1[6-9].*|http://172.2[0-9].*|http://172.3[0-1].*)
              echo "Backend {{BACKEND_URL}} is local - the in-stack builder owns merging on this install; exiting clean."
              echo "skip=1" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;;
          esac

      # Publish-mode gate: the DispatchSEO dashboard controls whether merging
      # is hands-off via the auto_merge automation flag (off in semi mode,
      # on in auto, per-toggle in custom). When it's off the merge step is
      # skipped and green PRs wait on the dashboard's ready-to-ship cards;
      # validation self-healing below still runs so tool PRs keep getting
      # their verdicts either way. A 404 means the backend predates the
      # endpoint - behave as before (merge). Anything else is a real failure
      # and must be loud, not a silent skip.
      - name: Look up the project's automation flags
        id: mode
        if: steps.guard.outputs.skip != '1'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/mode.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode)
          merge=on
          if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then
            if [ "$(jq -r '.automations.auto_merge' /tmp/mode.json)" = "false" ]; then merge=off; fi
            echo "Publish mode: $(jq -r '.mode' /tmp/mode.json) (auto_merge: $merge)"
          elif [ "$code" != "404" ]; then
            echo "::error::project-mode endpoint returned HTTP $code - check the DispatchSEO backend and SEO_MCP_API_KEY"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "merge=$merge" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Merge green SEO PRs
        id: merge
        if: steps.guard.outputs.skip != '1' && steps.mode.outputs.merge != 'off'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # A PR we cannot merge is REPORTED, never fatal. It used to exit 1
          # mid-loop, which killed the rest of the sweep - one guide PR with a
          # merge conflict stopped every later PR AND the stalled-tool-
          # validation step below from running at all (2026-08-02, usagecut).
          BLOCKED_FILE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/merge-blocked"
          : > "$BLOCKED_FILE"

          prs=$(gh pr list --repo "$REPO" --label seo --state open --json number --jq '.[].number')
          if [ -z "$prs" ]; then
            echo "No open SEO PRs. Nothing to do."
            exit 0
          fi

          # Publish dirs a guide PR may touch: the repo-owned config file on
          # the default branch, falling back to the reference-stack layout.
          # The file is deliberately NOT part of the pipeline pack - pack
          # updates overwrite workflows verbatim, and this repo's layout must
          # survive that (the 2026-07-23 lesson: an update reverted an
          # adapted gate and stranded a green guide PR unmerged for hours).
          prefixes=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/contents/.dispatchseo/publish-paths" \
            -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" 2>/dev/null \
            | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' || true)
          if [ -z "$prefixes" ]; then
            prefixes=$'src/content/blog/\nsrc/components/blog/\npublic/blog/covers/'
            echo "No .dispatchseo/publish-paths on the default branch - using the reference defaults."
          fi
          echo "Guide PRs may touch: $(echo "$prefixes" | tr '\n' ' ')"
          prefixes_json=$(printf '%s\n' "$prefixes" | jq -R . | jq -s .)

          for n in $prs; do
            echo "::group::PR #$n"

            # 1. Eligibility gate, by PR shape:
            #    - Tool PR (seo-tool label): must carry tool-validated - the
            #      live smoke-test's pass verdict - AND a successful
            #      seo-tool-validate run for the PR's exact head SHA (any
            #      write-token holder can apply a label; a workflow run result
            #      cannot be forged), AND touch no file on the denylist below.
            #      Tools legitimately touch registries/components, so there is
            #      no allowlist - only the paths that change how the repo
            #      builds, deploys or runs CI are refused.
            #    - Guide PR: every changed file must live under one of the
            #      allowed publish dirs above; anything else forces manual
            #      review.
            labels=$(gh pr view "$n" --repo "$REPO" --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')
            if [[ " $labels " == *" seo-tool "* ]]; then
              if [[ " $labels " != *" tool-validated "* ]]; then
                echo "PR #$n is a tool PR without a tool-validated verdict yet - waiting for validation."
                echo "::endgroup::"
                continue
              fi
              # Denylist: CI, dependency manifests/lockfiles, build and deploy
              # config, and DispatchSEO's own repo config. A tool never needs
              # these, and a change to any of them runs on every later build.
              # File names match at any depth, so a monorepo app's own
              # package.json or next.config is covered too.
              denied=$(gh pr view "$n" --repo "$REPO" --json files --jq '
                [.files[].path | select(
                  startswith(".github/") or startswith(".dispatchseo/") or
                  test("(^|/)(package\\.json|pnpm-lock\\.yaml|package-lock\\.json|yarn\\.lock|bun\\.lockb|bun\\.lock|vercel\\.json|\\.npmrc)$") or
                  test("(^|/)next\\.config\\.[^/]*$") or test("(^|/)Dockerfile[^/]*$")
                )] | join(" ")')
              if [ -n "$denied" ]; then
                echo "PR #$n is a tool PR that touches protected file(s): $denied - leaving for manual review."
                echo "::endgroup::"
                continue
              fi
              head_sha=$(gh pr view "$n" --repo "$REPO" --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)
              validated=$(gh run list --repo "$REPO" --workflow seo-tool-validate.yml --commit "$head_sha" \
                --status success --json databaseId --jq length) || validated=0
              if [ "${validated:-0}" -le 0 ]; then
                echo "PR #$n carries tool-validated but has no successful seo-tool-validate run for head $head_sha - waiting for validation."
                echo "::endgroup::"
                continue
              fi
              echo "PR #$n is a validated tool PR - checking the status rollup."
            else
              outside=$(gh pr view "$n" --repo "$REPO" --json files | jq --argjson prefixes "$prefixes_json" \
                '[.files[].path | . as $f | select(($prefixes | any($f | startswith(.))) | not)] | length')
              if [ "$outside" != "0" ]; then
                echo "PR #$n touches $outside file(s) outside the allowed publish dirs (structural change) - leaving for manual review. If these paths are part of this repo's normal guide layout, add them to .dispatchseo/publish-paths."
                echo "::endgroup::"
                continue
              fi
            fi

            # 2. Checks gate: classify the whole status rollup into one verdict.
            #    StatusContext -> .state ; CheckRun -> .status/.conclusion.
            verdict=$(gh pr view "$n" --repo "$REPO" --json statusCheckRollup --jq '
              [ .statusCheckRollup[] |
                if .__typename == "CheckRun" then
                  ( if .status != "COMPLETED" then "PENDING"
                    elif ((.conclusion // "") | ascii_upcase) as $c
                         | ($c == "SUCCESS" or $c == "NEUTRAL" or $c == "SKIPPED") then "SUCCESS"
                    else "FAIL" end )
                else
                  ( ((.state // "") | ascii_upcase) as $s |
                    if $s == "SUCCESS" then "SUCCESS"
                    elif ($s == "PENDING" or $s == "EXPECTED") then "PENDING"
                    else "FAIL" end )
                end
              ] as $s |
              if ($s | length) == 0 then "NOCHECKS"
              elif ($s | index("FAIL")) then "FAIL"
              elif ($s | index("PENDING")) then "PENDING"
              else "SUCCESS" end')

            case "$verdict" in
              SUCCESS)
                echo "PR #$n has all checks green - merging."
                # Grab the guide slugs BEFORE merging - the merge deletes the
                # branch. Layout-independent on purpose (any changed .mdx
                # file's basename is its slug), so it works with whatever
                # content home .dispatchseo/publish-paths names. Tool PRs
                # yield an empty list; the IndexNow run then skips
                # URL-polling and pings straight from the sitemap.
                slugs=$(gh pr view "$n" --repo "$REPO" --json files \
                  --jq '[.files[].path | select(test("\\.mdx$")) | split("/") | last | sub("\\.mdx$"; "")] | join(" ")')
                # Keep WHY the merge was refused: the causes send the owner to
                # completely different places, and a conflict (two guide PRs
                # open at once both appending to the content registry, or main
                # moving on under an older branch) has nothing to do with the
                # branch protection the old message blamed.
                if ! merge_err=$(gh pr merge "$n" --repo "$REPO" --squash --delete-branch 2>&1); then
                  # Self-heal the common case before reporting anything. Every
                  # guide PR appends to the same shared registry files, so any
                  # guide PR still open when something else merges comes back
                  # CONFLICTING - and nothing ever rebased it, so it sat red
                  # forever waiting on a human. Ask GitHub to merge the base
                  # branch in: it succeeds whenever the two sides touched
                  # different lines (the usual case - two appends in different
                  # places), and the PR merges on the next sweep. A genuine
                  # line-level conflict still 422s and falls through to the
                  # message below.
                  case "$merge_err" in
                    *"merge conflicts"*|*"not mergeable"*|*"Base branch was modified"*|*"not up to date"*)
                      if gh api -X PUT "repos/$REPO/pulls/$n/update-branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                        echo "PR #$n was out of date - updated it from the default branch; it merges on the next sweep."
                        echo "::endgroup::"
                        continue
                      fi ;;
                  esac
                  case "$merge_err" in
                    *"merge conflicts"*|*"not mergeable"*)
                      reason="guide PR #$n has conflicts with the default branch that need a human or an agent to resolve - the automatic branch update could not fix them" ;;
                    *"Base branch was modified"*|*"not up to date"*)
                      reason="guide PR #$n is behind the default branch and this repo requires branches to be up to date - update the branch and it merges on the next sweep" ;;
                    *"Required status check"*|*"protected branch"*|*"review"*)
                      reason="guide PR #$n is blocked by a branch protection rule (a required review or status check) - merge it on GitHub, or relax the rule" ;;
                    *)
                      reason="could not merge green guide PR #$n: $(echo "$merge_err" | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-200)" ;;
                  esac
                  echo "::warning::$reason"
                  printf '%s\n' "$reason" >> "$BLOCKED_FILE"
                  echo "::endgroup::"
                  continue
                fi
                # This squash push is made with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_TOKEN
                # pushes never trigger push-event workflows - so the IndexNow
                # workflow would silently skip every auto-merged guide.
                # Dispatch it explicitly (workflow_dispatch is the documented
                # exception to that rule).
                gh workflow run indexnow.yml --repo "$REPO" -f slugs="$slugs" \
                  || echo "IndexNow dispatch failed - the sitemap still covers the URL on the next crawl."
                ;;
              PENDING)
                echo "PR #$n has checks still running - will retry next run."
                ;;
              FAIL)
                echo "PR #$n has a failing check - leaving for the owner."
                ;;
              NOCHECKS)
                echo "PR #$n has no checks reported yet - not merging (no gate)."
                ;;
            esac
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

          # Hand the precise reason to the report step. Without this the
          # dashboard said only "workflow failed - <run url>", which is the
          # one thing the doctrine forbids: a failure whose detail exists
          # solely in an Actions log the owner has no reason to open.
          if [ -s "$BLOCKED_FILE" ]; then
            count=$(wc -l < "$BLOCKED_FILE" | tr -d ' ')
            msg=$(head -1 "$BLOCKED_FILE")
            [ "$count" -gt 1 ] && msg="$msg (and $((count - 1)) more PR(s) blocked the same way)"
            echo "blocked=$msg" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # Self-healing for the tool pipeline. Two ways a tool PR ends up with
      # no verdict label and would otherwise strand silently:
      # - The bot-PR approval gate (GitHub change, 2026-06-11): the builder
      #   opens PRs with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, so their pull_request
      #   validation runs are created parked in "action_required" and never
      #   execute. No repo setting disables that, and the approve API rejects
      #   same-repo PRs - but workflow_dispatch events created with
      #   GITHUB_TOKEN always run (the documented exception).
      # - A validator crash (max-turns, infra flake) that ended a run without
      #   applying any verdict label.
      # So each pass: for every verdict-less open tool PR with no validation
      # currently queued or running, dispatch a fresh validation on the PR's
      # branch (the dispatched run resolves and gates the PR itself).
      # Bounded: after 3 executed validations for the same head SHA with no
      # verdict, leave the PR for the owner instead of burning usage all day.
      - name: Dispatch stalled tool validations
        if: steps.guard.outputs.skip != '1'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          prs=$(gh pr list --repo "$REPO" --label seo-tool --state open \
            --json number,headRefName,headRefOid,labels \
            --jq '.[] | select([.labels[].name] | (index("tool-validated") or index("tool-validation-failed")) | not) | "\(.number) \(.headRefOid) \(.headRefName)"')
          if [ -z "$prs" ]; then
            echo "No verdict-less tool PRs. Nothing to do."
            exit 0
          fi

          while read -r n sha branch; do
            echo "::group::PR #$n"
            summary=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/seo-tool-validate.yml/runs?head_sha=$sha&per_page=30" \
              --jq '{active: ([.workflow_runs[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length), executed: ([.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "completed" and .conclusion != "action_required")] | length), parked: ([.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "completed" and .conclusion == "action_required")] | length)}')
            active=$(echo "$summary" | jq -r .active)
            executed=$(echo "$summary" | jq -r .executed)
            parked=$(echo "$summary" | jq -r .parked)
            echo "Validation runs for $sha: active=$active executed=$executed parked=$parked"
            if [ "$active" != "0" ]; then
              echo "A validation is already queued or running - waiting for its verdict."
            elif [ "$executed" -ge 3 ]; then
              echo "$executed validations executed with no verdict - leaving PR #$n for the owner."
              curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
                --data-urlencode "job=seo-tool-validate" \
                --data-urlencode "fail=tool PR #$n stranded: 3 validations produced no verdict - review it manually" \
                "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
            else
              echo "Dispatching a fresh validation on $branch (approval-gated or crashed run)."
              gh workflow run seo-tool-validate.yml --repo "$REPO" --ref "$branch" -f pr_number="$n" \
                || echo "::warning::Dispatch failed - if this branch predates the dispatch-mode validator, merge or validate PR #$n manually."
            fi
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done <<< "$prs"

      # Phone the outcome home: failures land on the DispatchSEO dashboard
      # banner + alert email (same rails as the crons); successes clear any
      # earlier red banner row for this job.
      - name: Report outcome to the dashboard
        if: always() && steps.guard.outputs.skip != '1'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ job.status }}
          BLOCKED: ${{ steps.merge.outputs.blocked }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} # names the failed step in the report
        run: |
          # A PR the sweep declined to merge is a real "needs you" state even
          # though the run itself is green - report the reason, not a run URL.
          if [ -n "$BLOCKED" ]; then
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-auto-merge" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=$BLOCKED" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          elif [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-auto-merge" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          else
            # Name the failing step so the alert email/banner says WHERE the run
            # died, not just that it did - the operator can't open a customer's
            # private Actions log, and "workflow failed" alone forced exactly
            # that dead end (2026-08-02). Best-effort: on any API hiccup the
            # message falls back to the bare form.
            step=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/jobs" \
              --jq '[.jobs[].steps[]? | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .name] | first // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-auto-merge" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=workflow failed${step:+ at step '$step'} - $RUN_URL" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          fi

name: SEO install canary

# Install-time proof that the whole PR machinery works. setup.sh dispatches
# this once at the end of an install: it creates a throwaway branch, opens a
# real PR from inside a workflow (the exact thing GitHub's default settings
# block on new repos), then closes it and deletes the branch - nothing is
# ever merged, no deploy is triggered. If any switch is wrong, the install
# fails HERE, in front of the owner, instead of on day 3 at 05:00.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  canary:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write # gh label create
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Open and close a throwaway PR from a workflow
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          branch="dispatchseo-canary-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -b "$branch"
          mkdir -p .dispatchseo
          echo "run ${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" > .dispatchseo/canary
          git add .dispatchseo/canary
          git commit -m "chore: DispatchSEO install canary (auto-closed, never merged)"
          git push origin "$branch"
          gh label create seo --color 0e8a16 --description "DispatchSEO SEO pipeline" 2>/dev/null || true
          gh label create seo-tool --color 1d76db --description "DispatchSEO tool PR" 2>/dev/null || true
          pr=$(gh pr create --title "DispatchSEO install canary (auto-closes)" \
            --body "Throwaway PR proving GitHub Actions may open pull requests on this repo. Closed automatically by the same run - never merge this." \
            --base "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --head "$branch" --label seo)
          echo "Canary PR created: $pr"
          gh pr close "$pr" --delete-branch
          echo "Canary PR closed and branch deleted - PR machinery verified."

      - name: Clean up the canary branch if the run failed
        if: failure()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          git push origin --delete "dispatchseo-canary-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" 2>/dev/null || true

      - name: Report result to the dashboard
        if: always()
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ job.status }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-canary" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          else
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-canary" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=install canary could not open a PR - enable 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' (repo Settings -> Actions -> General) and re-run setup" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          fi

name: SEO daily builder

# Every morning, build the oldest approved suggestion (guide or tool) into a PR,
# fully autonomously, through the centrally-served DispatchSEO pipeline (get_instructions -> template -> live
# SERP gate -> humanizer -> PR). If nothing is approved, it exits cleanly. Skips
# if an SEO PR is already open, so there is never more than one at a time - the
# steady state is build -> auto-merge -> gone -> repeat, and if a PR gets stuck
# (failed check, or a tool PR awaiting you) the builder pauses instead of piling
# more on top. Publishing is handled by seo-auto-merge.yml: guide PRs whose
# checks all pass are merged hands-off; tool PRs are left for you to merge.
#
# WOKEN BY THE BACKEND, not by a cron chain. The dashboard decides when a build
# is due and fires the seo-guide-build repository_dispatch (see
# api/cron/seo-dispatch) - it already knows whether anything is approved,
# whether a PR is still open, and whether today's guide is built, so it can
# answer all of that without starting a runner.
#
# This used to run three times a day (05:13, 12:13, 19:13 UTC): once to work,
# twice as insurance against GitHub's scheduler dropping a trigger and against
# a Claude usage-limit deferral. GitHub bills a full minute minimum for every
# job that claims a runner, so those two extra attempts cost real money on your
# account to re-discover, in the guard step below, something the dashboard
# already knew. The backend retries instead - its own scheduler ticks every few
# hours, and a deferred run simply stays due.
#
# The single cron below is a DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH, not the schedule. It covers the
# one case the backend cannot report on: the backend itself being down or
# unable to reach this repo, which would otherwise stop every dispatch with
# nothing left running to notice. It fires LATE in the day on purpose - by
# 19:13 a healthy backend has long since dispatched, so the guard below finds
# today's guide already built and exits in seconds.
#
# Daily rather than weekly, deliberately. A weekly switch is cheaper (~8 billed
# minutes a month against ~60) but it lets a dead backend cost up to six days
# of publishing on a product whose whole promise is a guide a day. One day is
# an acceptable worst case; six is not. Offset off the top of the hour: GitHub
# queues/drops on-the-hour triggers more than odd minutes.

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [seo-guide-build]
  schedule:
    - cron: "13 19 * * *" # 19:13 UTC - dead-man's switch only, see above
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: seo-build
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # continue-on-error at JOB level: a failure still runs the failure() steps
    # and still reports to the dashboard rails, but the RUN concludes green so
    # GitHub never emails the repo owner "Run failed". The dashboard Home
    # banner / get_cron_health are the alerting surface for these runs.
    continue-on-error: true
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read # the outcome report reads which step failed
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The agent commits below. Pin an identity that maps to a real GitHub
      # account - Vercel refuses to deploy commits from unknown author emails,
      # and an unconfigured runner leaves the agent to improvise one.
      - name: Pin git identity to github-actions[bot]
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Skip if an SEO PR is already open or guide builds are toggled off
        id: guard
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          # Tool PRs carry BOTH `seo` and `seo-tool`, and auto-merge never merges
          # a tool PR unattended - it waits for tool-validated AND the owner. So
          # counting them here let one unreviewed tool PR pause the entirely
          # separate GUIDE builder indefinitely, while every paused attempt
          # reported ok=1 and kept the dashboard green (2026-08-02). Guides are
          # blocked only by another guide PR.
          open=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --label seo --state open --json number,labels \
            --jq '[.[] | select([.labels[].name] | index("seo-tool") | not)] | length')
          if [ "$open" != "0" ]; then
            echo "A guide PR is already open - skipping this run so only one is ever open at a time."
            echo "skip_reason=a guide PR is already open and unmerged" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Automation-flag gate: the DispatchSEO dashboard can pause guide
          # builds (auto_build_guides off). 404 = backend without the endpoint
          # yet -> build as before; other failures are loud.
          if [ "$open" = "0" ]; then
            code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/mode.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
            if [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.automations.auto_build_guides' /tmp/mode.json)" = "false" ]; then
              echo "Guide builds are toggled off on the dashboard - skipping."
              open=paused
            elif [ "$code" = "unreachable" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ] || [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "503" ] || [ "$code" = "504" ]; then
              # Self-hosted backends reboot (kernel updates, docker restarts).
              # Unreachable is a delay, not a failure - the backend re-dispatches
              # on its next tick (the job stays due until something reports a
              # real outcome), and the in-stack builder covers this window too.
              echo "Backend unreachable right now (rebooting?) - deferring; it will re-dispatch when it is back."
              open=defer
              echo "skip_reason=the backend was unreachable, so this run was deferred" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            elif [ "$code" != "200" ] && [ "$code" != "404" ]; then
              echo "::error::project-mode endpoint returned HTTP $code"; exit 1
            fi
          fi
          # Already-built-today gate. The backend also checks cadence before it
          # dispatches, so this is the second of two gates, not the only one -
          # it still matters because workflow_dispatch, the daily dead-man's
          # cron, and a re-dispatch after an unreported run can all arrive on a
          # day that already has its guide.
          # Best-effort: missing field, non-200, or a parse failure all read
          # as "not built yet" so this check can never itself block a build.
          if [ "$open" = "0" ]; then
            code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/mode.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
            if [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.built_today.guide // false' /tmp/mode.json 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]; then
              echo "Today's guide is already built - skipping this attempt."
              open=skip
            fi
          fi
          # Empty-queue gate, and it belongs HERE rather than inside the agent
          # run. The backend never dispatches with an empty queue, so on the
          # normal path this is already known - but the dead-man's cron below
          # has no such knowledge, and without this it would start a full
          # coding-agent session every day on a project with nothing approved,
          # just to have the agent exit cleanly. That is the expensive shape of
          # the no-op this whole design removes.
          # Absent field (older backend) or any non-200 reads as "work is
          # waiting", so this can only ever cost a run, never suppress one.
          if [ "$open" = "0" ] && [ "$code" = "200" ]; then
            if [ "$(jq -r '.approved_waiting.guide // true' /tmp/mode.json 2>/dev/null)" = "false" ]; then
              echo "No approved guide suggestions are waiting - nothing to build."
              open=skip
            fi
          fi
          echo "open=$open" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # >>> agent-steps: resolve (GENERATED - edit scripts/agent-ci/ and regenerate; never edit between these markers)
      # Which coding agent runs this workflow - resolved at RUN time from the
      # dashboard, never baked in at install time. A decision left to whoever
      # ran the install is a decision someone eventually forgets, and the
      # failure mode here is a builder that runs the wrong agent every night.
      # Asking the backend means switching agent on the dashboard takes effect
      # on the next scheduled run with nothing to edit in this repo.
      #
      # The fallback matters as much as the happy path: a repo installed against
      # a backend that predates the `agent` field gets no value here, and must
      # keep behaving exactly as it did - which is claude, because Claude was
      # the only option that ever existed before the field.
      - name: Resolve the coding agent
        id: agent
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          CLAUDE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          agent=""
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/agent.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
          [ "$code" = "200" ] && agent=$(jq -r '.agent // empty' /tmp/agent.json 2>/dev/null)
          if [ -z "$agent" ] || [ "$agent" = "null" ]; then
            # No answer from the backend. Infer from which secret exists, and
            # tie-break to claude - see the note above.
            if [ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ] && [ -z "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then agent=codex
            elif [ -n "$CURSOR_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ] && [ -z "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then agent=cursor
            else agent=claude
            fi
            echo "Backend did not name an agent (HTTP $code) - inferred '$agent' from the secrets on this repo."
          fi
          # Fail here, in plain language, rather than letting the agent's own
          # action die minutes in on a cryptic validation error. The 2026-07-17
          # dogfood install burned four runs on exactly that.
          case "$agent" in
            claude)
              if [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ] && [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "No CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN on this repo - running Claude on the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret instead (metered API billing on your Anthropic account)."
              elif [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Claude Code, but the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret is missing or empty on this repo (and there is no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret to fall back on). Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard (it mints and VERIFIES a fresh token), or set one by hand: run 'claude setup-token', then pipe the token into 'gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN' without any whitespace. Or run on metered API billing instead: create a key at console.anthropic.com and pipe it into 'gh secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'."
                exit 1
              else
                case "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" in
                  sk-ant-oat*) : ;;
                  *)
                    echo "::error::CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN does not look like a Claude Code OAuth token (expected it to start with sk-ant-oat). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to mint and verify a replacement."
                    exit 1 ;;
                esac
                if [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then
                  echo "Both CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are set - the subscription token takes precedence. To run on the API key instead: gh secret delete CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN."
                fi
              fi ;;
            codex)
              if [ -z "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Codex, but the OPENAI_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. Add it with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY', or rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$OPENAI_API_KEY" in
                sk-*) : ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::OPENAI_API_KEY does not look like an OpenAI key (expected it to start with sk-). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Create a fresh key at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again."
                  exit 1 ;;
              esac ;;
            cursor)
              if [ -z "$CURSOR_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Cursor, but the CURSOR_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. A runner has no browser, so the interactive 'cursor-agent login' is not an option here - only an API key works. Mint one at cursor.com/dashboard/api (open the URL directly; any plan can) and add it with 'gh secret set CURSOR_API_KEY', or switch this project to Claude Code or Codex on your DispatchSEO dashboard."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$CURSOR_API_KEY" in
                sk-ant-*)
                  echo "::error::CURSOR_API_KEY holds a Claude credential (it starts with sk-ant-). The wrong secret was pasted. Put the Claude token in CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and a Cursor API key here."
                  exit 1 ;;
                sk-*)
                  echo "::error::CURSOR_API_KEY holds an OpenAI key (it starts with sk-). The wrong secret was pasted. Put the OpenAI key in OPENAI_API_KEY and a Cursor API key here."
                  exit 1 ;;
                *[[:space:]]*)
                  # [[:space:]], never a literal tab in the pattern: a tab
                  # character in generated YAML is invalid indentation, and
                  # pipeline-pack-lint fails the build on it.
                  echo "::error::CURSOR_API_KEY contains whitespace, which almost always means it was line-wrapped when it was copied. Re-copy the key and set it again with: printf '%s' \"\$KEY\" | tr -d '[:space:]' | gh secret set CURSOR_API_KEY"
                  exit 1 ;;
                *) : ;;
              esac ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::The dashboard reported an unknown agent '$agent'. This repo's workflows are older than that setting - re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to update them."
              exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "agent=$agent" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Building with: $agent"
      # <<< agent-steps: resolve


      # Fail loudly if the seo-manager MCP is unreachable. Without this, a
      # stale URL in mcp-ci.json makes Claude see an empty toolset and "exit
      # cleanly" - a green run that built nothing (2026-07-14 domain-move bug).
      - name: Preflight - seo-manager MCP reachable
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          url=$(node -e "console.log(require('./.github/mcp-ci.json').mcpServers['seo-manager'].url)")
          code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 -X POST "$url" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
            -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"tools/list"}')
          if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::seo-manager MCP at $url returned HTTP $code - fix the URL in .github/mcp-ci.json or the SEO_MCP_API_KEY secret"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "seo-manager MCP OK ($url)"

      # Deliberately NOT an INSTALL-ADAPT step. Which package manager this
      # repo uses is resolved at RUN time - packageManager pin first, then
      # lockfiles - never by an install-time edit, because an edit whose
      # omission is fatal is banned (scripts/pipeline-pack-lint.mjs; the
      # 2026-07-30 incident where a missed DELETE-this-line killed every
      # pinned repo's builder at step 2 is why). Assuming every repo is pnpm
      # was the same bug one layer up: the zero-touch cloud install commits
      # this pack verbatim into repos nobody adapted, and the first real
      # cloud customer's npm+Vite site died 25 seconds into every build
      # (2026-08-02). pnpm keeps its two blessed shapes (pinned reads the
      # pin, unpinned pins the action - a version input on a step that also
      # sees a packageManager pin is what hard-errors); npm/yarn/bun get
      # their own installs; no package.json at all skips Node setup entirely
      # and the agent works from the repo's real build story in
      # .dispatchseo/conventions.md.
      - name: Detect this repo's package manager
        id: pkg
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        run: |
          pm=none; pnpm_pinned=0; cache=""
          if [ -f package.json ]; then
            field=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(String(require("./package.json").packageManager || ""))' 2>/dev/null || true)
            case "$field" in
              pnpm@*) pm=pnpm; pnpm_pinned=1 ;;
              yarn@*) pm=yarn ;;
              npm@*)  pm=npm ;;
              bun@*)  pm=bun ;;
            esac
            if [ "$pm" = "none" ]; then
              if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then pm=pnpm
              elif [ -f package-lock.json ]; then pm=npm
              elif [ -f yarn.lock ]; then pm=yarn
              elif [ -f bun.lock ] || [ -f bun.lockb ]; then pm=bun
              else pm=npm
              fi
            fi
          fi
          # setup-node's cache input hard-errors when the matching lockfile is
          # missing, so only request a cache that provably exists.
          case "$pm" in
            pnpm) if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then cache=pnpm; fi ;;
            npm)  if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then cache=npm; fi ;;
            yarn) if [ -f yarn.lock ]; then cache=yarn; fi ;;
          esac
          # Node major, resolved at RUN time - same rule and same reason as the
          # package manager above. `node-version: 22` was hardcoded here while
          # the install playbook told the installing agent to hand-edit it if
          # the repo built on something else, which is the banned shape exactly:
          # a pack update pushes this file VERBATIM, so that edit self-reverts
          # on the next sync and the builder then dies on the wrong major in a
          # repo nobody is watching (2026-08-02).
          #
          # .nvmrc first - a repo that ships one has DECLARED the version its
          # own developers build on, so it is honoured as written. engines.node
          # is read as a FLOOR rather than a target: ">=18" is a minimum a Node
          # 22 runner already satisfies, and resolving it downward would move
          # working installs onto an EOL major - and below pnpm 11's own floor -
          # to satisfy a constraint that was never violated. 22 when neither
          # file says anything, which is what every install already runs, so a
          # repo that declares nothing sees no change at all.
          node_v=22
          if [ -f .nvmrc ]; then
            # Tolerates "v22", "22.11.0" and trailing whitespace; an alias like
            # "lts/*" names no number, so the default stands.
            v=$(grep -Eo '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+){0,2}' .nvmrc 2>/dev/null | head -1)
            [ -n "$v" ] && node_v="$v"
          elif [ -f package.json ]; then
            eng=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(String((require("./package.json").engines||{}).node||""))' 2>/dev/null || true)
            major=$(printf '%s' "$eng" | grep -Eo '[0-9]+' | head -1)
            if [ -n "$major" ] && [ "$major" -gt 22 ]; then node_v="$major"; fi
          fi
          { echo "pm=$pm"; echo "pnpm_pinned=$pnpm_pinned"; echo "cache=$cache"; echo "node=$node_v"; } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "package manager: $pm (pnpm pin: $pnpm_pinned, node cache: ${cache:-off}, node: $node_v)"

      # Pinned -> action-setup reads the exact version out of the field.
      # Passing a version input as well is precisely what hard-errors.
      - name: Set up pnpm (version from the repo's packageManager pin)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pkg.outputs.pm == 'pnpm' && steps.pkg.outputs.pnpm_pinned == '1'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4

      # No pin -> action-setup has to be told. pnpm 11 matches the Node 22
      # floor resolved above; a repo whose lockfile was written by an older
      # major should add a packageManager field rather than edit this, which
      # routes it to the exact path above.
      - name: Set up pnpm (no packageManager pin in this repo)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pkg.outputs.pm == 'pnpm' && steps.pkg.outputs.pnpm_pinned == '0'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4
        with:
          version: 11

      - name: Set up Bun
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pkg.outputs.pm == 'bun'
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2

      - name: Set up Node
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pkg.outputs.pm != 'none'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          # Resolved by the detection step above, never hand-edited - see the
          # comment there for why an install-time edit could not stay applied.
          node-version: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.node }}
          cache: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.cache }}

      - name: Install deps (so the agent's build/verify step works)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pkg.outputs.pm != 'none'
        env:
          PM: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.pm }}
        run: |
          case "$PM" in
            pnpm)
              pnpm install --frozen-lockfile || {
                s=$?
                echo "::error::pnpm install failed (exit $s). Frequent causes: (1) ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS - pnpm 11 hard-fails dependencies with unanswered build scripts (strictDepBuilds is on by default): answer each one in pnpm-workspace.yaml (allowBuilds: dep: true/false, plus an onlyBuiltDependencies list for older pnpm) and commit. (2) pnpm/lockfile version mismatch - align the workflow's pnpm with the version that wrote pnpm-lock.yaml (package.json packageManager field). Reproduce locally with a fresh 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile'."
                exit $s
              } ;;
            npm)
              { if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then npm ci || npm install; else npm install; fi; } || {
                s=$?
                echo "::error::npm install failed (exit $s). Reproduce locally with a fresh 'npm ci' (or 'npm install' if the lockfile is stale) and commit whatever lockfile change it produces."
                exit $s
              } ;;
            yarn)
              corepack enable 2>/dev/null || true
              { yarn install --immutable || yarn install; } || {
                s=$?
                echo "::error::yarn install failed (exit $s). Reproduce locally with 'yarn install' and commit the lockfile it produces."
                exit $s
              } ;;
            bun)
              bun install || {
                s=$?
                echo "::error::bun install failed (exit $s). Reproduce locally with 'bun install'."
                exit $s
              } ;;
          esac

      # >>> agent-steps: run (GENERATED - edit scripts/agent-ci/ and regenerate; never edit between these markers)
      # Codex reads its MCP servers from a config.toml inside its own home
      # directory. Two things here are easy to get wrong and both are silent:
      #
      # 1. The action does NOT honour an inbound CODEX_HOME env var - it takes a
      #    `codex-home` INPUT and sets the env itself. Writing a config to a
      #    hand-rolled $CODEX_HOME and hoping is a no-op, and the failure looks
      #    like an agent with no tools rather than an error.
      # 2. `sandbox: workspace-write` blocks network by default, which kills MCP
      #    over HTTP. The network_access line below is what makes the sandboxed
      #    posture usable at all.
      - name: Write Codex's MCP config
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        env:
          DATAFORSEO_LOGIN: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN }}
          DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home"
          cp .github/mcp-codex.toml "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml"
          cat >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml" <<'TOML'

          [sandbox_workspace_write]
          network_access = true
          TOML
          # Render the DataForSEO credential tokens. Codex's TOML `env` map is
          # LITERAL - it does not expand ${VAR} the way Claude expands its JSON
          # config - so left alone the dataforseo server would authenticate as
          # the literal string "${DATAFORSEO_LOGIN}" and every keyword call
          # would 401 mid-build. python3 rather than sed so no credential
          # character can break the substitution; values are TOML-escaped. A
          # truncated config (free-mode project, no dataforseo section) makes
          # this a no-op.
          python3 - "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml" <<'PY'
          import os, sys
          path = sys.argv[1]
          text = open(path).read()
          for token, var in (("${DATAFORSEO_LOGIN}", "DATAFORSEO_LOGIN"),
                             ("${DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD}", "DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD")):
              val = os.environ.get(var, "").replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
              text = text.replace(token, val)
          open(path, "w").write(text)
          PY
          echo "Codex home prepared. Servers configured:"
          grep -E '^\[mcp_servers\.' "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml"

      # Cursor has no GitHub Action, so the CLI is installed here. Pinned to a
      # known version rather than piping cursor.com/install, which floats.
      #
      # Then the MCP config. The pack's mcp-ci.json is ALREADY Cursor's shape,
      # but its ${VAR} placeholders are rendered to real values here anyway.
      # Live runs (2026-08-06) showed cursor-agent CAN resolve ${VAR} in an
      # http server's headers from its own environment - which quietly carried
      # builds for a day while this render step was a no-op - but that
      # behaviour is undocumented and unproven for stdio env values, so the
      # credentials are never left to depend on it.
      #
      # `mcp enable` is not optional either. An unapproved server is not merely
      # unreachable, it is absent - the agent runs happily with zero tools.
      - name: Install Cursor and write its MCP config
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'cursor'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          DATAFORSEO_LOGIN: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN }}
          DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          # The WHOLE package, into a directory of its own. cursor-agent is a
          # bash launcher rather than a static binary and loads ~95 sibling
          # files from beside itself, so extracting just the executable gives a
          # command that exists and cannot run. Its own directory keeps those
          # 95 files out of $RUNNER_TEMP, which this job also uses for the
          # prompt and the result.
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-cli" "$HOME/.local/bin"
          curl -fsSL "https://downloads.cursor.com/lab/2026.07.23-e383d2b/linux/x64/agent-cli-package.tar.gz" \
            | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-cli"
          ln -sf "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-cli/cursor-agent" "$HOME/.local/bin/cursor-agent"
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          cursor-agent --version

          # python3, not sed: a credential can contain any character, and this
          # writes JSON, so the values are JSON-escaped rather than pasted.
          mkdir -p .cursor
          python3 - .github/mcp-ci.json .cursor/mcp.json <<'PY'
          import json, os, sys
          src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
          text = open(src).read()
          for var in ("SEO_MCP_API_KEY", "DATAFORSEO_LOGIN", "DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD"):
              # json.dumps then strip the quotes: escapes exactly what JSON
              # needs escaping and nothing else.
              val = json.dumps(os.environ.get(var, ""))[1:-1]
              text = text.replace("${" + var + "}", val)
          cfg = json.loads(text)
          json.dump(cfg, open(dst, "w"), indent=2)
          print("servers configured:", ", ".join(cfg.get("mcpServers", {})))
          PY

          # Approve every server the config declares. Per-directory state, so a
          # fresh checkout has none of it and this runs every time.
          for s in $(python3 -c "import json;print(' '.join(json.load(open('.cursor/mcp.json')).get('mcpServers',{})))"); do
            cursor-agent mcp enable "$s"
          done
          echo "--- mcp list ---"
          cursor-agent mcp list

      - name: Run the SEO builder
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'claude'
        id: claude
        # Never fail the job at this step: the classify step below reads the
        # outcome and decides what the run MEANS (transient rate limit vs dead
        # account), which it can only do if it is reachable.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@61a9c274fa7110a66dfafc1bbbced03833eb25fe # v1
        with:
          # Cloud fires this as the DispatchSEO GitHub App (a Bot actor), and the App also authored the workflow commits, so scheduled runs are bot-actored too. Every trigger here needs repo write access, so allowing bots is safe; without this claude-code-action aborts with "non-human actor".
          allowed_bots: "*"
          # Subscription token first; the metered ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only reaches
          # the action when no subscription token exists, so adding a key never
          # silently switches a working subscription install to per-token billing.
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN == '' && secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY || '' }}
          # Pass the standard workflow token as an input so the action uses it
          # directly instead of exchanging OIDC for a Claude GitHub App token
          # (which would require installing the app on the repo).
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          prompt: |
            FIRST call the seo-manager MCP tool get_instructions with workflow build-guide, then follow the returned markdown exactly - it is the current playbook and overrides any cached knowledge of this pipeline. Also read .dispatchseo/conventions.md for this repo's site facts. In brief: take the oldest approved guide suggestion, mark it in_progress, build the guide MDX through the full pipeline (template, thin-content gate, draft, mandatory visuals, humanizer), run pnpm build to verify, open a PR labeled seo via gh, then update_suggestion to done with the PR url and log_page, and state the instructions version in the run report. Never build tool suggestions - those belong to the seo-build-tool workflow. If get_instructions is unavailable, fail loudly and exit without changes; if there are no approved guide suggestions, exit cleanly without any changes.
          claude_args: |
            --mcp-config ./.github/mcp-ci.json
            --permission-mode bypassPermissions
            --max-turns 150
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN == '' && secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY || '' }}
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          DATAFORSEO_LOGIN: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN }}
          DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          MCP_TIMEOUT: "120000"
          # Placeholder public env so `next build` never trips on missing vars -
          # static blog pages do not call Supabase, and the clients are lazy.
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: "https://placeholder.supabase.co"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: "placeholder-anon-key"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: "https://{{DOMAIN}}"

      # The Codex twin. Same task prompt, generated from the same source -
      # the agent's behaviour must not depend on which one is holding the
      # playbook - plus the unattended-environment preamble above it.
      #
      # Model: gpt-5 by default, overridable with a repo variable because model
      # availability is per-account, not universal - `gpt-5-codex` 404s on a
      # pay-as-you-go project key even though it appears in GET /v1/models. Set
      # SEO_CODEX_MODEL in the repo's Actions variables to change it without
      # touching this file.
      #
      # There is NO turn budget to set. Codex has no --max-turns equivalent and
      # OpenAI closed the request for one as not-planned, so the job's
      # timeout-minutes is the only ceiling on a runaway run.
      - name: Run the SEO builder (Codex)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        id: codex
        # Never fail the job at this step: the classify step below reads the
        # outcome and decides what the run MEANS (transient rate limit vs dead
        # account), which it can only do if it is reachable.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: openai/codex-action@bdf19a4a223ec2549a3e2274a0cf61556bc07675 # v1
        with:
          openai-api-key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          # Same rule as the Claude twin's allowed_bots: this workflow is fired
          # by a bot actor (the DispatchSEO GitHub App, a schedule, or a
          # GITHUB_TOKEN dispatch). codex-action's actor gate rejects EVERY bot
          # by default (a bot 404s the collaborator-permission lookup), so
          # without this line each unattended Codex run dies before Codex is
          # even installed - while a manual workflow_dispatch passes, which is
          # what hides the failure. Every trigger that can reach this step
          # already required repo write access, so allowing all actors adds
          # nothing an attacker can use.
          allow-users: "*"
          model: ${{ vars.SEO_CODEX_MODEL || 'gpt-5' }}
          codex-home: ${{ runner.temp }}/codex-home
          sandbox: workspace-write
          # Strips sudo from the runner user for the rest of the job. Safe here:
          # everything after this step is curl. It is also more than the Claude
          # half of this pipeline does, which runs with bypassPermissions and no
          # sandbox at all.
          safety-strategy: drop-sudo
          output-file: ${{ runner.temp }}/codex-out.txt
          prompt: |
            ENVIRONMENT RULE (read first, it overrides habit): you have no apply_patch tool here - only the shell, and you are running UNATTENDED, so there is nobody to answer a question. Write every file with a SINGLE-QUOTED heredoc (cat > path <<'DSEOF' ... DSEOF) or with python3 reading the content from stdin. The quoted delimiter is the whole point: bash expands NOTHING inside it, so the backticks and $ in MDX and TSX survive verbatim. NEVER use an unquoted heredoc, printf or echo to write file content - an unquoted heredoc is what expands backticks and corrupts the file. Pick a delimiter that cannot appear in the content. Verify every write with ls -l and head before moving on, and never let a filename come from an unset shell variable. If you ever find yourself about to ask for approval or a go/no-go, do not: pick the safest option that still completes the task, do it, and say what you chose in the final report. A run that stops to ask a question builds nothing and is a failed run.

            FIRST call the seo-manager MCP tool get_instructions with workflow build-guide, then follow the returned markdown exactly - it is the current playbook and overrides any cached knowledge of this pipeline. Also read .dispatchseo/conventions.md for this repo's site facts. In brief: take the oldest approved guide suggestion, mark it in_progress, build the guide MDX through the full pipeline (template, thin-content gate, draft, mandatory visuals, humanizer), run pnpm build to verify, open a PR labeled seo via gh, then update_suggestion to done with the PR url and log_page, and state the instructions version in the run report. Never build tool suggestions - those belong to the seo-build-tool workflow. If get_instructions is unavailable, fail loudly and exit without changes; if there are no approved guide suggestions, exit cleanly without any changes.
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          DATAFORSEO_LOGIN: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN }}
          DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: "https://placeholder.supabase.co"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: "placeholder-anon-key"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: "https://{{DOMAIN}}"

      # The Cursor twin. Same task prompt, generated from the same source -
      # the agent's behaviour must not depend on which one is holding the
      # playbook - plus the unattended-environment preamble above it.
      #
      # A plain run step, because Cursor ships no GitHub Action. The three
      # flags are each separately required and each was measured: --trust (a
      # fresh checkout is an untrusted workspace and the run refuses outright),
      # --force (command approval), --approve-mcps (server approval).
      #
      # --output-format json is what makes the classify step below honest: it
      # returns {is_error, subtype, result, usage}, so a failure is read from a
      # field rather than guessed at from warning text.
      #
      # Model is overridable per repo: availability is per-account, and the
      # account default ("auto") is the sane fallback. There is NO turn budget
      # to set - Cursor has no --max-turns equivalent, so the job's
      # timeout-minutes is the only ceiling on a runaway run, and on Cursor a
      # runaway also eats the plan's monthly usage pool.
      - name: Run the SEO builder (Cursor)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'cursor'
        id: cursor
        # Never fail the job at this step: the classify step below reads the
        # outcome and decides what the run MEANS (transient limit vs dead
        # account), which it can only do if it is reachable.
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          DATAFORSEO_LOGIN: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN }}
          DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: "https://placeholder.supabase.co"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: "placeholder-anon-key"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: "https://{{DOMAIN}}"
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-prompt.txt" <<'DSEOF'
          ENVIRONMENT RULE (read first, it overrides habit): you are running UNATTENDED on a CI runner. There is nobody here to answer a question, approve a step, or pick between options. If you ever find yourself about to ask for approval or a go/no-go, do not: choose the safest option that still completes the task, do it, and say what you chose in the final report. A run that stops to ask a question builds nothing and is a failed run. Your final message is read by a script, so end with exactly what you were asked to end with and nothing after it.

          FIRST call the seo-manager MCP tool get_instructions with workflow build-guide, then follow the returned markdown exactly - it is the current playbook and overrides any cached knowledge of this pipeline. Also read .dispatchseo/conventions.md for this repo's site facts. In brief: take the oldest approved guide suggestion, mark it in_progress, build the guide MDX through the full pipeline (template, thin-content gate, draft, mandatory visuals, humanizer), run pnpm build to verify, open a PR labeled seo via gh, then update_suggestion to done with the PR url and log_page, and state the instructions version in the run report. Never build tool suggestions - those belong to the seo-build-tool workflow. If get_instructions is unavailable, fail loudly and exit without changes; if there are no approved guide suggestions, exit cleanly without any changes.
          DSEOF
          set +e
          cursor-agent -p "$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-prompt.txt")" \
            --output-format json --trust --force --approve-mcps \
            --model "${{ vars.SEO_CURSOR_MODEL || 'auto' }}" \
            > "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-out.json" 2> "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-err.txt"
          code=$?
          set -e
          # The final message, for the classify step. jq tolerates a truncated
          # or absent file, which is what a killed run leaves behind.
          jq -r '.result // empty' "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-out.json" 2>/dev/null > "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-msg.txt" || true
          echo "--- cursor exit $code ---"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-msg.txt"
          [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-err.txt" ] && { echo "--- stderr ---"; cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-err.txt"; }
          exit $code

      # Turn-by-turn detail for tuning the pipeline. The dashboard only ever
      # receives the aggregate outcome, which cannot answer the question that
      # actually matters for cost - WHICH pipeline steps burn the turns. This
      # step is what makes that measurable, since the agent run is ~98% of this
      # job's billed wall clock and wall clock is turns x per-turn latency.
      #
      # PRIVATE REPOS ONLY, and that condition is the point rather than
      # caution. Artifacts on a public repository are downloadable by anyone,
      # and this file is the agent's execution log - which is exactly why the
      # classify step below reads it instead of printing it ("these logs can be
      # public"). Publishing it as an artifact would undo that decision for the
      # public repos we specifically recommend to people avoiding Actions
      # charges. Short retention because this is a debugging aid, not a record.
      - name: Save the agent execution log for turn analysis
        if: always() && steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && github.event.repository.private
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: agent-execution-log-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/claude-execution-output.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/codex-out.txt
            ${{ runner.temp }}/cursor-out.json
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # Decide what the run MEANS before anything is reported. The agent steps
      # run with continue-on-error so this step is reachable either way; it
      # reads the final result/error message the agent left behind: a genuine
      # usage-limit hit is not a pipeline failure, it is deferred (the dashboard
      # keeps the job due and re-dispatches within hours) and reported as a
      # GREEN run. Anything else is reported red with the real reason. GitHub's
      # secret masking still applies to whatever prints.
      - name: Classify the outcome
        id: classify
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          CODEX_MSG: ${{ steps.codex.outputs.final-message }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          AGENT: ${{ steps.agent.outputs.agent }}
          AGENT_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex' && steps.codex.outcome || steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'cursor' && steps.cursor.outcome || steps.claude.outcome }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          # Mirror the per-agent step outcome into an output, so the report
          # step's condition never has to name agent step ids.
          echo "agent_outcome=${AGENT_OUTCOME:-}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Pull whatever the agent left behind.
          msg=""
          if [ "$AGENT" = "codex" ]; then
            msg="$CODEX_MSG"
            [ -n "$msg" ] || msg=$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-out.txt" 2>/dev/null)
          elif [ "$AGENT" = "cursor" ]; then
            msg=$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-msg.txt" 2>/dev/null || true)
            [ -n "$msg" ] || msg=$(jq -r '.result // empty' "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-out.json" 2>/dev/null)
          else
            f="$RUNNER_TEMP/claude-execution-output.json"
            if [ -f "$f" ]; then
              msg=$(jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[] else . end
                           | select(.type? == "result")
                           | (.result // .error // empty)' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
            fi
          fi

          # A deferral is reported as `deferred`, NOT as ok. The difference
          # decides whether this job's work happens today at all: the dashboard
          # works out what is due by reading these reports, and an `ok` row is a
          # COMPLETED run - it would start the full cadence window over and
          # suppress the retry, so an evening usage limit would silently cost a
          # day while the dashboard showed green. `deferred` says "ran, built
          # nothing", which keeps the job due and gets it re-dispatched within
          # hours.
          defer() {
