            echo "This project builds with Codex, but the OPENAI_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. Add it with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY', or re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"
            cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"; exit 1
          fi
          code=$(curl -s --max-time 30 -o /tmp/live.json -w "%{http_code}" https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d '{"model":"gpt-5-mini","input":"ok","max_output_tokens":16}') || code=000
          err=$(jq -r '.error.code // empty' /tmp/live.json 2>/dev/null)
          case "$code:$err" in
            2*:*) echo "OpenAI key is live." ; exit 0 ;;
            429:rate_limit_exceeded)
              # Transient by definition. A health check that goes red on a
              # momentary rate limit trains people to ignore the banner.
              echo "OpenAI is rate-limiting this key right now - that clears by itself, so treating it as healthy." ; exit 0 ;;
            429:*|402:*)
              echo "your OpenAI account cannot run builds (OpenAI said: ${err:-quota exceeded}). Retrying will not fix this - add credit or raise the limit at platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt" ;;
            401:*|403:*)
              echo "OpenAI rejected the OPENAI_API_KEY secret on this repo (HTTP $code). The key was probably revoked or rotated - create a new one at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY'." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt" ;;
            *)
              echo "could not reach OpenAI to check the key (HTTP $code)." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt" ;;
          esac
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"; exit 1

      # Measured trap, and the reason this looks paranoid: `cursor-agent models`
      # exits 0 even when the API key is invalid, and `cursor-agent status`
      # ignores CURSOR_API_KEY altogether (it reports the interactive login,
      # which a runner does not have). Both obvious checks therefore pass for
      # every broken key that will ever exist. This one reads the text.
      - name: Cursor key liveness
        id: liveness_cursor
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'cursor'
        env:
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$CURSOR_API_KEY" ]; then
            echo "This project builds with Cursor, but the CURSOR_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. A runner has no browser, so 'cursor-agent login' is not an option - only an API key works. Mint one at cursor.com/dashboard/api (any plan can) and add it with 'gh secret set CURSOR_API_KEY', or switch this project to Claude Code or Codex on your dashboard." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"
            cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"; exit 1
          fi
          # Whole package into its own directory - the launcher needs its
          # siblings; see the config step for the long version.
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-cli"
          curl -fsSL "https://downloads.cursor.com/lab/2026.07.23-e383d2b/linux/x64/agent-cli-package.tar.gz" \
            | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-cli"
          out=$("$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-cli/cursor-agent" models 2>&1) || true
          if printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qi "API key is invalid\|Authentication required\|Unauthorized"; then
            echo "Cursor rejected the CURSOR_API_KEY secret on this repo. The key was probably revoked, or the plan's usage pool is exhausted. Mint a fresh key at cursor.com/dashboard/api and set it again with 'gh secret set CURSOR_API_KEY'." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"
            cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"; exit 1
          fi
          if ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Available models"; then
            echo "Could not check the Cursor key - the CLI answered with something unrecognised: $(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -c 300)" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"
            cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"; exit 1
          fi
          echo "Cursor key is live."
      # <<< agent-steps: liveness


      - name: Report token OK
        if: success()
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            --data-urlencode "job=seo-token-check" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
            "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true

      # >>> agent-steps: failure-report (GENERATED - edit scripts/agent-ci/ and regenerate; never edit between these markers)
      # Surface the real API error (revoked? usage limit?) and phone it home.
      # Full transcripts stay hidden - only the final result line is read.
      - name: Report token failure with the reason
        if: failure()
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          AGENT: ${{ steps.agent.outputs.agent }}
        run: |
          reason="credential check failed (no error detail captured)"
          fix="re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard"
          if [ "$AGENT" = "codex" ]; then
            # The Codex branch already resolved OpenAI's own error code into a
            # sentence naming the actual fix, so pass that through rather than
            # flattening it back into a generic message.
            msg=$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt" 2>/dev/null)
            [ -n "$msg" ] && reason="Codex credential check failed: $msg"
          elif [ "$AGENT" = "cursor" ]; then
            # The Cursor branch already resolved this into a sentence naming the
            # actual fix, so pass that through rather than flattening it.
            msg=$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt" 2>/dev/null)
            [ -n "$msg" ] && reason="Cursor credential check failed: $msg"
          else
            f="$RUNNER_TEMP/claude-execution-output.json"
            if [ -f "$f" ]; then
              msg=$(jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[] else . end
                           | select(.type? == "result")
                           | (.result // .error // empty)' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
              [ -n "$msg" ] && reason="Claude token check failed: $msg"
            fi
            if echo "$msg" | grep -qiE 'session limit|usage limit|limit reached|limit .*resets|rate.?limit'; then
              # The credential WORKS - the account is just out of headroom right
              # now. The builders already treat that as a quiet deferral, so a
              # red health banner here would only train owners to ignore it.
              echo "Claude is usage-limited right now, but the credential itself is alive - treating the check as healthy. Builds defer until the limit resets."
              curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
                --data-urlencode "job=seo-token-check" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
                "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
              exit 0
            fi
            fix="mint a fresh token (claude setup-token) and re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard"
            if echo "$msg" | grep -qi 'disabled Claude subscription access'; then
              # oauth_org_not_allowed: a server-side flag on the ACCOUNT, not
              # the token - re-minting provably does nothing.
              fix="a fresh token will NOT fix this one - Anthropic has flagged the Claude account itself (oauth_org_not_allowed). On a company Claude plan, ask its admin to enable Claude Code; on a personal plan, check claude.ai billing for a lapsed or duplicate subscription or contact Anthropic support. Or switch the builders to metered API billing: create a key at console.anthropic.com, 'gh secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', then 'gh secret delete CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN'"
            fi
          fi
          echo "::error::$reason - $fix."
          curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            --data-urlencode "job=seo-token-check" \
            --data-urlencode "fail=$reason - $fix" \
            "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
      # <<< agent-steps: failure-report


      # Pipeline staleness: compare this repo's installed pack version stamp
      # against the backend's current one. Stale is not broken - the report
      # tells the owner an update is waiting; re-running the setup command
      # applies it. Repos installed before version stamps skip silently. A
      # non-200/404 response (401, 5xx, timeout) means the project key itself
      # is rejected, not that pipeline_version is unsupported - that must be
      # loud, not folded into the same silent skip.
      - name: Pipeline update check
        if: always()
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          [ -f .dispatchseo/pipeline-version ] || { echo "No version stamp (pre-stamp install) - skipping."; exit 0; }
          installed=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < .dispatchseo/pipeline-version)
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/mode.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode")
          if [ "$code" = "404" ]; then
            echo "Backend has no pipeline_version yet - skipping."
            exit 0
          elif [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::project-mode returned HTTP $code - the project key looks rejected by the backend. Re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to mint a fresh key."
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-token-check" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=project key rejected by backend (HTTP $code) - re-run the setup command" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
            exit 1
          fi
          current=$(jq -r '.pipeline_version // empty' /tmp/mode.json)
          if [ -z "$current" ]; then echo "Backend has no pipeline_version yet - skipping."; exit 0; fi
          if [ "$installed" = "$current" ]; then
            echo "Pipeline up to date ($installed)."
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-pipeline-version" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          else
            echo "::warning::Pipeline update available (installed $installed, current $current). Re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to apply it."
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-pipeline-version" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=pipeline update available (installed $installed, current $current) - re-run the setup command to apply" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          fi

name: SEO tool validation

# The functional reviewer for autonomously-built tool PRs. A tool PR may only
# auto-merge if this workflow has exercised the LIVE page (real production
# build, real browser) and proven the widget works. On pass it labels the PR
# `tool-validated`; the auto-merge gate requires that label for any PR that
# carries `seo-tool`. On fail it labels `tool-validation-failed` and comments
# the concrete failures so the next builder run (or the owner) can fix them.
#
# Scope: runs ONLY on same-repo PRs labeled seo-tool (the tool builder's PRs).
# Guide PRs never get the seo-tool label and are never gated by this.
#
# Two triggers for the same validation:
# - pull_request: the normal path. BUT tool PRs are opened by the builder
#   with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, and since GitHub's 2026-06-11 change
#   those runs are created parked in "action_required" (awaiting manual
#   approval, with no repo-level opt-out) - left alone the PR stalls forever.
# - workflow_dispatch (pr_number input): the escape hatch. Dispatch events
#   created with GITHUB_TOKEN always execute (documented exception), so
#   seo-auto-merge's self-heal dispatches this workflow for any verdict-less
#   tool PR. Both paths converge on the resolve step below, which re-verifies
#   the same-repo + seo-tool gates from live PR state.

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pr_number:
        description: "Open seo-tool PR number to validate"
        required: true

concurrency:
  group: seo-tool-validate-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  validate:
    # pull_request mode: same-repo PRs only (fork PRs get no secrets anyway)
    # + must be a tool PR. Dispatch mode passes here and is gated by the
    # resolve step instead (its event payload has no PR fields to check).
    if: >
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
       contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'seo-tool'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # SECURITY: this job builds and RUNS the PR's (LLM-authored) code, so it
    # must never hold a token that can write to the repo. Labels/comments only;
    # the squash-merge lives in the separate `merge` job below, which never
    # checks out or executes PR code.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write # gh label create
    steps:
      # Authoritative gate for BOTH trigger modes: read the PR's live state
      # and refuse anything that is not an open, same-repo, seo-tool PR. Also
      # resolves the head SHA the job checks out, so a dispatched run
      # validates exactly the PR head (not the default branch the dispatch
      # technically runs against).
      - name: Resolve and gate the PR
        id: pr
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}
        run: |
          case "$PR_NUMBER" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "::error::pr_number must be a plain PR number."; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          info=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --json state,isCrossRepository,labels,headRefOid \
            --jq '{state, cross: .isCrossRepository, labels: [.labels[].name], sha: .headRefOid}')
          echo "$info"
          if [ "$(echo "$info" | jq -r .state)" != "OPEN" ] \
             || [ "$(echo "$info" | jq -r .cross)" != "false" ] \
             || ! echo "$info" | jq -e '.labels | index("seo-tool")' >/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::PR #$PR_NUMBER is not an open same-repo seo-tool PR - refusing to validate."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "sha=$(echo "$info" | jq -r .sha)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # The resolved PR head, so both trigger modes exercise the same code.
          ref: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.sha }}
          # Don't leave a git credential on disk for the PR's build scripts to
          # read - this job's steps talk to GitHub only via the env tokens on
          # the specific steps that need them.
          persist-credentials: false

      # >>> agent-steps: resolve (GENERATED - edit scripts/agent-ci/ and regenerate; never edit between these markers)
      # Which coding agent validates, plus the fail-fast on a broken credential.
      # Both agents get the same plain-language error rather than dying minutes
      # in on a cryptic validation failure.
      #
      # UNLIKE every other workflow, this one does NOT ask the backend which
      # agent to use. Asking means holding SEO_MCP_API_KEY, and the one thing
      # this job must never do is acquire a reason to hold the project key - it
      # builds and RUNS the PR's (LLM-authored) code. A secret is only visible
      # to the step that names it, so the leak would not be direct - but the
      # invariant is worth more than the consistency.
      #
      # The SEO_AGENT repo VARIABLE is the primary answer. Variables (unlike
      # secrets) are readable without holding anything sensitive, and the
      # backend best-effort writes this one on every agent switch and install,
      # so this workflow can agree with the dashboard without asking it.
      # Inference from secret presence remains the fallback for repos whose
      # backend predates the variable - but on its own it was NOT just
      # cosmetic: switching agents leaves the old secret behind (the switch is
      # deliberately a single column write), the tie-break below then picks the
      # default, and if the owner switched because that agent's account lapsed,
      # validation goes red and every tool PR on the project strands unmerged.
      - name: Resolve the coding agent
        id: agent
        env:
          CLAUDE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          AGENT_VAR: ${{ vars.SEO_AGENT }}
        run: |
          case "$AGENT_VAR" in
            claude|codex|cursor) agent="$AGENT_VAR" ;;
            *)
              if [ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ] && [ -z "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then agent=codex
              elif [ -n "$CURSOR_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ] && [ -z "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then agent=cursor
              else agent=claude
              fi
              ;;
          esac
          case "$agent" in
            claude)
              if [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ] && [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "No CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN on this repo - running Claude on the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret instead (metered API billing on your Anthropic account)."
              elif [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project validates with Claude Code, but the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret is missing or empty on this repo (and there is no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret to fall back on). Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard (it mints and VERIFIES a fresh token), or set one by hand: run 'claude setup-token', then pipe the token into 'gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN' without any whitespace. Or run on metered API billing instead: create a key at console.anthropic.com and pipe it into 'gh secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'."
                exit 1
              else
                case "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" in
                  sk-ant-oat*) : ;;
                  *)
                    echo "::error::CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN does not look like a Claude Code OAuth token (expected it to start with sk-ant-oat). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to mint and verify a replacement."
                    exit 1 ;;
                esac
                if [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then
                  echo "Both CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are set - the subscription token takes precedence. To run on the API key instead: gh secret delete CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN."
                fi
              fi ;;
            codex)
              if [ -z "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project validates with Codex, but the OPENAI_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. Add it with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY', or rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$OPENAI_API_KEY" in
                sk-*) : ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::OPENAI_API_KEY does not look like an OpenAI key (expected it to start with sk-). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Create a fresh key at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again."
                  exit 1 ;;
              esac ;;
            cursor)
              if [ -z "$CURSOR_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project validates with Cursor, but the CURSOR_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. A runner has no browser, so the interactive 'cursor-agent login' is not an option here - only an API key works. Mint one at cursor.com/dashboard/api (open the URL directly; any plan can) and add it with 'gh secret set CURSOR_API_KEY', or switch this project to Claude Code or Codex on your DispatchSEO dashboard."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$CURSOR_API_KEY" in
                sk-ant-*)
                  echo "::error::CURSOR_API_KEY holds a Claude credential (it starts with sk-ant-). The wrong secret was pasted. Put the Claude token in CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and a Cursor API key here."
                  exit 1 ;;
                sk-*)
                  echo "::error::CURSOR_API_KEY holds an OpenAI key (it starts with sk-). The wrong secret was pasted. Put the OpenAI key in OPENAI_API_KEY and a Cursor API key here."
                  exit 1 ;;
                *[[:space:]]*)
                  # [[:space:]], never a literal tab in the pattern: a tab
                  # character in generated YAML is invalid indentation, and
                  # pipeline-pack-lint fails the build on it.
                  echo "::error::CURSOR_API_KEY contains whitespace, which almost always means it was line-wrapped when it was copied. Re-copy the key and set it again with: printf '%s' \"\$KEY\" | tr -d '[:space:]' | gh secret set CURSOR_API_KEY"
                  exit 1 ;;
                *) : ;;
              esac ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::The dashboard reported an unknown agent '$agent'. This repo's workflows are older than that setting - re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to update them."
              exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "agent=$agent" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Validating with: $agent"
      # <<< agent-steps: resolve


      # Deliberately NOT an INSTALL-ADAPT step. Which package manager this
      # repo uses is resolved at RUN time - packageManager pin first, then
      # lockfiles - never by an install-time edit, because an edit whose
      # omission is fatal is banned (scripts/pipeline-pack-lint.mjs; the
      # 2026-07-30 incident where a missed DELETE-this-line killed every
      # pinned repo's builder at step 2 is why). Assuming every repo is pnpm
      # was the same bug one layer up: the zero-touch cloud install commits
      # this pack verbatim into repos nobody adapted, and the first real
      # cloud customer's npm+Vite site died 25 seconds into every build
      # (2026-08-02). pnpm keeps its two blessed shapes (pinned reads the
      # pin, unpinned pins the action - a version input on a step that also
      # sees a packageManager pin is what hard-errors); npm/yarn/bun get
      # their own installs; no package.json at all skips Node setup entirely
      # and the agent works from the repo's real build story in
      # .dispatchseo/conventions.md.
      - name: Detect this repo's package manager
        id: pkg
        run: |
          pm=none; pnpm_pinned=0; cache=""
          if [ -f package.json ]; then
            field=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(String(require("./package.json").packageManager || ""))' 2>/dev/null || true)
            case "$field" in
              pnpm@*) pm=pnpm; pnpm_pinned=1 ;;
              yarn@*) pm=yarn ;;
              npm@*)  pm=npm ;;
              bun@*)  pm=bun ;;
            esac
            if [ "$pm" = "none" ]; then
              if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then pm=pnpm
              elif [ -f package-lock.json ]; then pm=npm
              elif [ -f yarn.lock ]; then pm=yarn
              elif [ -f bun.lock ] || [ -f bun.lockb ]; then pm=bun
              else pm=npm
              fi
            fi
          fi
          # setup-node's cache input hard-errors when the matching lockfile is
          # missing, so only request a cache that provably exists.
          case "$pm" in
            pnpm) if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then cache=pnpm; fi ;;
            npm)  if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then cache=npm; fi ;;
            yarn) if [ -f yarn.lock ]; then cache=yarn; fi ;;
          esac
          # Node major, resolved at RUN time - same rule and same reason as the
          # package manager above. `node-version: 22` was hardcoded here while
          # the install playbook told the installing agent to hand-edit it if
          # the repo built on something else, which is the banned shape exactly:
          # a pack update pushes this file VERBATIM, so that edit self-reverts
          # on the next sync and the builder then dies on the wrong major in a
          # repo nobody is watching (2026-08-02).
          #
          # .nvmrc first - a repo that ships one has DECLARED the version its
          # own developers build on, so it is honoured as written. engines.node
          # is read as a FLOOR rather than a target: ">=18" is a minimum a Node
          # 22 runner already satisfies, and resolving it downward would move
          # working installs onto an EOL major - and below pnpm 11's own floor -
          # to satisfy a constraint that was never violated. 22 when neither
          # file says anything, which is what every install already runs, so a
          # repo that declares nothing sees no change at all.
          node_v=22
          if [ -f .nvmrc ]; then
            # Tolerates "v22", "22.11.0" and trailing whitespace; an alias like
            # "lts/*" names no number, so the default stands.
            v=$(grep -Eo '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+){0,2}' .nvmrc 2>/dev/null | head -1)
            [ -n "$v" ] && node_v="$v"
          elif [ -f package.json ]; then
            eng=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(String((require("./package.json").engines||{}).node||""))' 2>/dev/null || true)
            major=$(printf '%s' "$eng" | grep -Eo '[0-9]+' | head -1)
            if [ -n "$major" ] && [ "$major" -gt 22 ]; then node_v="$major"; fi
          fi
          { echo "pm=$pm"; echo "pnpm_pinned=$pnpm_pinned"; echo "cache=$cache"; echo "node=$node_v"; } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "package manager: $pm (pnpm pin: $pnpm_pinned, node cache: ${cache:-off}, node: $node_v)"

      # Pinned -> action-setup reads the exact version out of the field.
      # Passing a version input as well is precisely what hard-errors.
      - name: Set up pnpm (version from the repo's packageManager pin)
        if: steps.pkg.outputs.pm == 'pnpm' && steps.pkg.outputs.pnpm_pinned == '1'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4

      # No pin -> action-setup has to be told. pnpm 11 matches the Node 22
      # floor resolved above; a repo whose lockfile was written by an older
      # major should add a packageManager field rather than edit this, which
      # routes it to the exact path above.
      - name: Set up pnpm (no packageManager pin in this repo)
        if: steps.pkg.outputs.pm == 'pnpm' && steps.pkg.outputs.pnpm_pinned == '0'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4
        with:
          version: 11

      - name: Set up Bun
        if: steps.pkg.outputs.pm == 'bun'
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2

      - name: Set up Node
        if: steps.pkg.outputs.pm != 'none'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          # Resolved by the detection step above, never hand-edited - see the
          # comment there for why an install-time edit could not stay applied.
          node-version: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.node }}
          cache: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.cache }}

      - name: Install deps
        if: steps.pkg.outputs.pm != 'none'
        env:
          PM: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.pm }}
        run: |
          case "$PM" in
            pnpm)
              pnpm install --frozen-lockfile || {
                s=$?
                echo "::error::pnpm install failed (exit $s). Frequent causes: (1) ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS - pnpm 11 hard-fails dependencies with unanswered build scripts (strictDepBuilds is on by default): answer each one in pnpm-workspace.yaml (allowBuilds: dep: true/false, plus an onlyBuiltDependencies list for older pnpm) and commit. (2) pnpm/lockfile version mismatch - align the workflow's pnpm with the version that wrote pnpm-lock.yaml (package.json packageManager field). Reproduce locally with a fresh 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile'."
                exit $s
              } ;;
            npm)
              { if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then npm ci || npm install; else npm install; fi; } || {
                s=$?
                echo "::error::npm install failed (exit $s). Reproduce locally with a fresh 'npm ci' (or 'npm install' if the lockfile is stale) and commit whatever lockfile change it produces."
                exit $s
              } ;;
            yarn)
              corepack enable 2>/dev/null || true
              { yarn install --immutable || yarn install; } || {
                s=$?
                echo "::error::yarn install failed (exit $s). Reproduce locally with 'yarn install' and commit the lockfile it produces."
                exit $s
              } ;;
            bun)
              bun install || {
                s=$?
                echo "::error::bun install failed (exit $s). Reproduce locally with 'bun install'."
                exit $s
              } ;;
          esac

      - name: Production build
        if: steps.pkg.outputs.pm != 'none'
        run: |
          case "${{ steps.pkg.outputs.pm }}" in
            pnpm) pnpm build ;;
            npm)  npm run build ;;
            yarn) yarn build ;;
            bun)  bun run build ;;
          esac
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: "https://placeholder.supabase.co"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: "placeholder-anon-key"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: "http://localhost:3000"

      # How a repo serves a production build is repo-specific: Next's `start`
      # on 3000, Vite's `preview` on 4173, Hugo's `server` on 1313, a static
      # `python3 -m http.server`. Resolve it at RUN TIME from a repo-owned
      # file - never by hand-editing this workflow at install. Two incidents
      # are why: 2026-07-30 a missed install-time edit killed the builder in
      # every repo with a `packageManager` pin, and the fix for it left THIS
      # step still hardcoded to `run start` on :3000, so any non-Next stack
      # failed every tool PR with "server never answered on :3000" while the
      # only remedy lived in a prose line of the install playbook. Like
      # .dispatchseo/publish-paths, this file is deliberately outside the
      # pack, so a pack update can never revert the adaptation.
      #
      # .dispatchseo/serve - one KEY=VALUE per line, # comments allowed:
      #   command=npm run preview -- --port 4173
      #   port=4173
      - name: Resolve how this repo serves a production build
        id: serve
        run: |
          cmd=""; port=""
          if [ -f .dispatchseo/serve ]; then
            cmd=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*command=//p' .dispatchseo/serve | head -1)
            port=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*port=//p' .dispatchseo/serve | head -1)
          fi
          # Default only where there IS a package.json to run a script from.
          if [ -z "$cmd" ] && [ "$PM" != "none" ]; then cmd="$PM run start"; fi
          port="${port:-3000}"
          if [ -z "$cmd" ]; then
            echo "::error::This repo has no package.json, so there is no default way to serve its built site for tool validation. Create .dispatchseo/serve on the default branch with two lines - command=<what serves the production build> and port=<the port it listens on> - and commit it. That file is repo-owned: pipeline updates never overwrite it."
            exit 1
          fi
          { echo "command=$cmd"; echo "port=$port"; echo "base=http://localhost:$port"; } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "serving with: $cmd (expecting :$port)"
        env:
          PM: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.pm }}

      # Readiness, not correctness: ANY HTTP answer proves the server is
      # listening, so the only thing this waits out is curl's 000 (nothing on
      # the port yet). Demanding 200 from `/` strands every site whose home
      # page does not serve one - an app behind a login, a locale bounce, a
      # marketing root that 30x's - and it fails in the most misleading way
      # available: the log says the server is ready, then says it never
      # started. It stranded DispatchSEO's own PR #25 for three runs on
      # 2026-08-02. Whether the app actually works is the agent's call, made
      # against the tool's own page further down - never this probe's.
      - name: Start server and wait for it
        env:
          SERVE_CMD: ${{ steps.serve.outputs.command }}
          SERVE_PORT: ${{ steps.serve.outputs.port }}
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: "https://placeholder.supabase.co"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: "placeholder-anon-key"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: ${{ steps.serve.outputs.base }}
        run: |
          nohup sh -c "$SERVE_CMD" >/tmp/serve.log 2>&1 &
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:$SERVE_PORT/" || true)
            case "$code" in
              ""|000) : ;;
              *) echo "server up (HTTP $code from /)"; exit 0 ;;
            esac
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "::error::'$SERVE_CMD' never answered on :$SERVE_PORT. If this repo serves differently, put the right command and port in .dispatchseo/serve on the default branch."
          cat /tmp/serve.log; exit 1

      - name: Install Playwright browser for the MCP
        run: npx -y playwright install --with-deps chromium

      # >>> agent-steps: run (GENERATED - edit scripts/agent-ci/ and regenerate; never edit between these markers)
      # Codex's twin of mcp-validate.json. Written here rather than shipped as a
      # file because this job's MCP surface is one stdio server with no secrets
      # in it - there is nothing to personalize per project, so a file would be
      # a second thing to keep in sync for no benefit.
      - name: Write Codex's MCP config
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home"
          cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml" <<'TOML'
          [mcp_servers.playwright]
          command = "npx"
          args = ["-y", "@playwright/mcp@latest", "--headless", "--isolated"]
          # Nobody is here to approve a tool call on a scheduled runner, and
          # without this every call comes back "user cancelled MCP tool call".
          default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"

          [sandbox_workspace_write]
          # The validator drives a real browser against the repo's own local
          # server, whose port came from .dispatchseo/serve.
          network_access = true
          TOML

      # Cursor has no GitHub Action, so the CLI is installed here. Pinned to a
      # known version rather than piping cursor.com/install, which floats.
      #
      # Then the MCP config. The pack's mcp-ci.json is ALREADY Cursor's shape,
      # but its ${VAR} placeholders are rendered to real values here anyway.
      # Live runs (2026-08-06) showed cursor-agent CAN resolve ${VAR} in an
      # http server's headers from its own environment - which quietly carried
      # builds for a day while this render step was a no-op - but that
      # behaviour is undocumented and unproven for stdio env values, so the
      # credentials are never left to depend on it.
      #
      # `mcp enable` is not optional either. An unapproved server is not merely
      # unreachable, it is absent - the agent runs happily with zero tools.
      - name: Install Cursor and write its MCP config
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'cursor'
        run: |
          # The WHOLE package, into a directory of its own. cursor-agent is a
          # bash launcher rather than a static binary and loads ~95 sibling
          # files from beside itself, so extracting just the executable gives a
          # command that exists and cannot run. Its own directory keeps those
          # 95 files out of $RUNNER_TEMP, which this job also uses for the
          # prompt and the result.
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-cli" "$HOME/.local/bin"
          curl -fsSL "https://downloads.cursor.com/lab/2026.07.23-e383d2b/linux/x64/agent-cli-package.tar.gz" \
            | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-cli"
          ln -sf "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-cli/cursor-agent" "$HOME/.local/bin/cursor-agent"
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          cursor-agent --version

          # python3, not sed: a credential can contain any character, and this
          # writes JSON, so the values are JSON-escaped rather than pasted.
          mkdir -p .cursor
          python3 - .github/mcp-validate.json .cursor/mcp.json <<'PY'
          import json, os, sys
          src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
          text = open(src).read()
          for var in ("SEO_MCP_API_KEY", "DATAFORSEO_LOGIN", "DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD"):
              # json.dumps then strip the quotes: escapes exactly what JSON
              # needs escaping and nothing else.
              val = json.dumps(os.environ.get(var, ""))[1:-1]
              text = text.replace("${" + var + "}", val)
          cfg = json.loads(text)
          json.dump(cfg, open(dst, "w"), indent=2)
          print("servers configured:", ", ".join(cfg.get("mcpServers", {})))
          PY

          # Approve every server the config declares. Per-directory state, so a
          # fresh checkout has none of it and this runs every time.
          for s in $(python3 -c "import json;print(' '.join(json.load(open('.cursor/mcp.json')).get('mcpServers',{})))"); do
            cursor-agent mcp enable "$s"
          done
          echo "--- mcp list ---"
          cursor-agent mcp list

      - name: Validate the tool live
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'claude'
        id: claude
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@61a9c274fa7110a66dfafc1bbbced03833eb25fe # v1
        with:
          # Tool PRs are opened and pushed by the builder workflow, so the
          # triggering actor is github-actions[bot]; without this the action
          # refuses to start ("non-human actor") and the PR never gets a
          # verdict. Same-repo + seo-tool label gates above still apply.
          allowed_bots: "github-actions"
          # Subscription token first; the metered ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only reaches
          # the action when no subscription token exists, so adding a key never
          # silently switches a working subscription install to per-token billing.
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN == '' && secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY || '' }}
          # Pass the standard workflow token as an input so the action uses it
          # directly instead of exchanging OIDC for a Claude GitHub App token
          # (which would require installing the app on the repo).
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Full transcript in the step log - post-hoc debuggability.
          show_full_output: true
          prompt: |
            You are the functional validator for an autonomously-built {{SITE_NAME}} tool PR. 1) Find the tool under review: run `git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` and read the diff of the tools registry (its path is listed in .dispatchseo/conventions.md) to get the NEW tool's slug (the entry added in this PR). 2) Work out the tool's PUBLIC path - never assume /tools/<slug>: take it from the route/page files the PR added, the registry entry's own path field, or the Tools section of .dispatchseo/conventions.md, and cross-check it against the sitemap. (Sites whose /tools route belongs to a logged-in app publish elsewhere, e.g. /free-tools/<slug>; a login redirect or 404 here means you have the wrong path, not a broken tool - re-derive it before judging.) Using the playwright MCP, open ${{ steps.serve.outputs.base }}<path> and validate: the page returns 200 and renders the landing funnel (hero h1, the interactive widget, FAQ section); every primary widget interaction works (fill each input with realistic values, click every action button, verify output actually updates, test the copy action); edge cases do not break it (empty input, nonsense input - the widget must never throw); zero console errors during the whole session (check browser console messages). 3) Verdict: if EVERYTHING passes, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated --remove-label tool-validation-failed || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated` and post a short PR comment via `gh pr comment` summarizing what you exercised. If ANYTHING fails, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed --remove-label tool-validated || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed` (removing tool-validated matters: a stale pass from an earlier commit must not authorize a merge) and comment the concrete failures (what you did, what happened, console output). Create missing labels with `gh label create` if needed. The PR number is in the PR_NUMBER environment variable. Never modify code in this run - you are a reviewer only.
          claude_args: |
            --mcp-config ./.github/mcp-validate.json
            --permission-mode bypassPermissions
            --max-turns 140
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN == '' && secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY || '' }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}

      # The Codex twin. Same task prompt, generated from the same source -
      # the agent's behaviour must not depend on which one is holding the
      # playbook - plus the unattended-environment preamble above it.
      #
      # Model: gpt-5 by default, overridable with a repo variable because model
      # availability is per-account, not universal - `gpt-5-codex` 404s on a
      # pay-as-you-go project key even though it appears in GET /v1/models. Set
      # SEO_CODEX_MODEL in the repo's Actions variables to change it without
      # touching this file.
      #
      # There is NO turn budget to set. Codex has no --max-turns equivalent and
      # OpenAI closed the request for one as not-planned, so the job's
      # timeout-minutes is the only ceiling on a runaway run.
      - name: Validate the tool live (Codex)
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        id: codex
        uses: openai/codex-action@bdf19a4a223ec2549a3e2274a0cf61556bc07675 # v1
        with:
          openai-api-key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          # Same rule as the Claude twin's allowed_bots: this workflow is fired
          # by a bot actor (the DispatchSEO GitHub App, a schedule, or a
          # GITHUB_TOKEN dispatch). codex-action's actor gate rejects EVERY bot
          # by default (a bot 404s the collaborator-permission lookup), so
          # without this line each unattended Codex run dies before Codex is
          # even installed - while a manual workflow_dispatch passes, which is
          # what hides the failure. Every trigger that can reach this step
          # already required repo write access, so allowing all actors adds
          # nothing an attacker can use.
          allow-users: "*"
          model: ${{ vars.SEO_CODEX_MODEL || 'gpt-5' }}
          codex-home: ${{ runner.temp }}/codex-home
          sandbox: workspace-write
          # Strips sudo from the runner user for the rest of the job. Safe here:
          # everything after this step is curl. It is also more than the Claude
          # half of this pipeline does, which runs with bypassPermissions and no
          # sandbox at all.
          safety-strategy: drop-sudo
          output-file: ${{ runner.temp }}/codex-out.txt
          prompt: |
            ENVIRONMENT RULE (read first, it overrides habit): you have no apply_patch tool here - only the shell, and you are running UNATTENDED, so there is nobody to answer a question. Write every file with a SINGLE-QUOTED heredoc (cat > path <<'DSEOF' ... DSEOF) or with python3 reading the content from stdin. The quoted delimiter is the whole point: bash expands NOTHING inside it, so the backticks and $ in MDX and TSX survive verbatim. NEVER use an unquoted heredoc, printf or echo to write file content - an unquoted heredoc is what expands backticks and corrupts the file. Pick a delimiter that cannot appear in the content. Verify every write with ls -l and head before moving on, and never let a filename come from an unset shell variable. If you ever find yourself about to ask for approval or a go/no-go, do not: pick the safest option that still completes the task, do it, and say what you chose in the final report. A run that stops to ask a question builds nothing and is a failed run.

            You are the functional validator for an autonomously-built {{SITE_NAME}} tool PR. 1) Find the tool under review: run `git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` and read the diff of the tools registry (its path is listed in .dispatchseo/conventions.md) to get the NEW tool's slug (the entry added in this PR). 2) Work out the tool's PUBLIC path - never assume /tools/<slug>: take it from the route/page files the PR added, the registry entry's own path field, or the Tools section of .dispatchseo/conventions.md, and cross-check it against the sitemap. (Sites whose /tools route belongs to a logged-in app publish elsewhere, e.g. /free-tools/<slug>; a login redirect or 404 here means you have the wrong path, not a broken tool - re-derive it before judging.) Using the playwright MCP, open ${{ steps.serve.outputs.base }}<path> and validate: the page returns 200 and renders the landing funnel (hero h1, the interactive widget, FAQ section); every primary widget interaction works (fill each input with realistic values, click every action button, verify output actually updates, test the copy action); edge cases do not break it (empty input, nonsense input - the widget must never throw); zero console errors during the whole session (check browser console messages). 3) Verdict: if EVERYTHING passes, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated --remove-label tool-validation-failed || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated` and post a short PR comment via `gh pr comment` summarizing what you exercised. If ANYTHING fails, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed --remove-label tool-validated || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed` (removing tool-validated matters: a stale pass from an earlier commit must not authorize a merge) and comment the concrete failures (what you did, what happened, console output). Create missing labels with `gh label create` if needed. The PR number is in the PR_NUMBER environment variable. Never modify code in this run - you are a reviewer only.
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}

      # The Cursor twin. Same task prompt, generated from the same source -
      # the agent's behaviour must not depend on which one is holding the
      # playbook - plus the unattended-environment preamble above it.
      #
      # A plain run step, because Cursor ships no GitHub Action. The three
      # flags are each separately required and each was measured: --trust (a
      # fresh checkout is an untrusted workspace and the run refuses outright),
      # --force (command approval), --approve-mcps (server approval).
      #
      # --output-format json is what makes the classify step below honest: it
      # returns {is_error, subtype, result, usage}, so a failure is read from a
      # field rather than guessed at from warning text.
      #
      # Model is overridable per repo: availability is per-account, and the
      # account default ("auto") is the sane fallback. There is NO turn budget
      # to set - Cursor has no --max-turns equivalent, so the job's
      # timeout-minutes is the only ceiling on a runaway run, and on Cursor a
      # runaway also eats the plan's monthly usage pool.
      - name: Validate the tool live (Cursor)
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'cursor'
        id: cursor
        env:
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-prompt.txt" <<'DSEOF'
          ENVIRONMENT RULE (read first, it overrides habit): you are running UNATTENDED on a CI runner. There is nobody here to answer a question, approve a step, or pick between options. If you ever find yourself about to ask for approval or a go/no-go, do not: choose the safest option that still completes the task, do it, and say what you chose in the final report. A run that stops to ask a question builds nothing and is a failed run. Your final message is read by a script, so end with exactly what you were asked to end with and nothing after it.

          You are the functional validator for an autonomously-built {{SITE_NAME}} tool PR. 1) Find the tool under review: run `git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` and read the diff of the tools registry (its path is listed in .dispatchseo/conventions.md) to get the NEW tool's slug (the entry added in this PR). 2) Work out the tool's PUBLIC path - never assume /tools/<slug>: take it from the route/page files the PR added, the registry entry's own path field, or the Tools section of .dispatchseo/conventions.md, and cross-check it against the sitemap. (Sites whose /tools route belongs to a logged-in app publish elsewhere, e.g. /free-tools/<slug>; a login redirect or 404 here means you have the wrong path, not a broken tool - re-derive it before judging.) Using the playwright MCP, open ${{ steps.serve.outputs.base }}<path> and validate: the page returns 200 and renders the landing funnel (hero h1, the interactive widget, FAQ section); every primary widget interaction works (fill each input with realistic values, click every action button, verify output actually updates, test the copy action); edge cases do not break it (empty input, nonsense input - the widget must never throw); zero console errors during the whole session (check browser console messages). 3) Verdict: if EVERYTHING passes, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated --remove-label tool-validation-failed || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated` and post a short PR comment via `gh pr comment` summarizing what you exercised. If ANYTHING fails, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed --remove-label tool-validated || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed` (removing tool-validated matters: a stale pass from an earlier commit must not authorize a merge) and comment the concrete failures (what you did, what happened, console output). Create missing labels with `gh label create` if needed. The PR number is in the PR_NUMBER environment variable. Never modify code in this run - you are a reviewer only.
          DSEOF
          set +e
          cursor-agent -p "$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-prompt.txt")" \
            --output-format json --trust --force --approve-mcps \
            --model "${{ vars.SEO_CURSOR_MODEL || 'auto' }}" \
            > "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-out.json" 2> "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-err.txt"
          code=$?
          set -e
          # The final message, for the classify step. jq tolerates a truncated
          # or absent file, which is what a killed run leaves behind.
          jq -r '.result // empty' "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-out.json" 2>/dev/null > "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-msg.txt" || true
          echo "--- cursor exit $code ---"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-msg.txt"
          [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-err.txt" ] && { echo "--- stderr ---"; cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/cursor-err.txt"; }
          exit $code
      # <<< agent-steps: run


      # NO report step here, on purpose: this job builds and RUNS the PR's
      # (LLM-authored) code, so it must hold no secrets at all - not even the
      # project MCP key. Outcome reporting lives in the merge job below,
      # which runs on a fresh runner with no checkout and no untrusted code.

  # The hands-off publish for tools: a PASS verdict from the live validation
  # above IS the merge authorization (the tool was built in prod mode and
  # exercised in a real browser - a stronger gate than any preview check).
  # FAIL or no verdict leaves the PR open for the owner.
  #
  # SECURITY: this is a separate job on a fresh runner precisely so the
  # contents:write token never coexists with the PR's executed code (the
  # validate job above builds and runs the branch). No checkout here - it only
  # reads labels and merges via gh.
  merge:
    needs: validate
    # Dispatch mode passes here by design: the validate job's resolve step
    # already enforced the same-repo + seo-tool gates, and this job re-reads
    # the labels via gh before acting anyway. always() so a FAILED validate
    # still reaches the report step below instead of silently skipping this
    # job - a red validation must land on the dashboard banner.
    if: >
      always() &&
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
       contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'seo-tool')))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: write # squash-merge + branch delete
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      # Phone the validation outcome home from THIS job - never from the
      # validate job, which executes the PR's (LLM-authored) code and must
      # hold no secrets. Failures land on the DispatchSEO dashboard banner +
      # alert email (same rails as the crons); successes clear any earlier
      # red banner row. A skipped validate (non-tool PR) reports nothing.
      - name: Report validation outcome to the dashboard
        if: needs.validate.result == 'success' || needs.validate.result == 'failure'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          VALIDATE_RESULT: ${{ needs.validate.result }}
        run: |
          if [ "$VALIDATE_RESULT" = "success" ]; then
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-tool-validate" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          else
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-tool-validate" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=validation workflow failed - $RUN_URL" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          fi

      - name: Merge on PASS verdict
        if: needs.validate.result == 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          # Publish-mode gate: same rule as seo-auto-merge - when the owner
          # turned auto_merge off (semi mode or a custom toggle), a PASS still
          # labels the PR but the merge waits for the dashboard's Merge click.
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/mode.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
          if [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.automations.auto_merge' /tmp/mode.json)" = "false" ]; then
            echo "auto_merge is off on the dashboard - leaving the validated PR for the owner."
            exit 0
          elif [ "$code" = "unreachable" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ] || [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "503" ] || [ "$code" = "504" ]; then
            # Local-backend self-host: a GitHub-hosted runner cannot reach a
            # localhost dashboard to read auto_merge. install.ts keeps this
            # workflow ENABLED on local backends, so don't crash - the tool is
            # already built and browser-validated; leave the labeled PR for the
            # dashboard / in-stack builder to merge (matches seo-daily.yml).
            echo "Backend unreachable (local self-host?) - leaving the validated PR for the dashboard to merge."
            exit 0
          elif [ "$code" != "200" ] && [ "$code" != "404" ]; then
            echo "::error::project-mode endpoint returned HTTP $code"; exit 1
          fi

          labels=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '.labels[].name')
          # Both conditions: tool-validated present AND no failure flag. A stale
          # tool-validated from an earlier commit must never merge a newer,
          # failing state of the branch.
          if echo "$labels" | grep -qx "tool-validated" && ! echo "$labels" | grep -qx "tool-validation-failed"; then
            echo "Validated - squash-merging PR #$PR_NUMBER."
            gh pr merge "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --squash --delete-branch || {
              gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --body "Validation passed but auto-merge failed (likely a conflict with main). Manual merge needed."
              # A merge failure used to die invisibly in this job - report it
              # so the banner + email say the PR is waiting on a human.
              curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
                --data-urlencode "job=seo-tool-validate" \
                --data-urlencode "fail=validation passed but auto-merge failed (likely a conflict with main) - PR left open for manual merge" \
                "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
              exit 1
            }
            # The squash push above is made with GITHUB_TOKEN, which never
            # triggers push-event workflows - dispatch IndexNow explicitly so
            # the new tool URL gets pinged (no blog slugs; the ping reads the
            # live sitemap).
            gh workflow run indexnow.yml --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              || echo "IndexNow dispatch failed - the sitemap still covers the URL on the next crawl."
          else
            echo "No tool-validated label - leaving the PR open for review."
          fi

name: SEO tool builder

# Builds the oldest APPROVED tool suggestion into a PR through the seo-manager
# skill's /seo-build-tool pipeline (claude-md-generator template -> live SERP
# gate -> theme discovery -> execution plan + value bar -> build -> humanizer
# -> PR labeled seo + seo-tool).
#
# Tools are approve-idea-first: nothing builds until the user greenlights the
# concept on the dashboard. Three triggers:
#   1. repository_dispatch "seo-tool-approved" - fired both the moment a tool
#      suggestion is approved AND by the backend's scheduler when the weekly
#      cadence comes due with something approved waiting (api/cron/seo-dispatch).
#      This is the real schedule now.
#   2. Weekly cron (Wednesday 19:42 UTC) - a DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH for a backend
#      that cannot dispatch at all. It was three crons (05:42, 12:42, 19:42)
#      purely to self-heal a trigger GitHub might drop; the backend re-fires
#      until a run reports back, so the other two were paying GitHub's
#      one-minute-minimum to discover there was nothing to do.
#   3. workflow_dispatch - manual runs.
# If the queue has no approved tools, the run exits cleanly - and the backend
# will not dispatch at all in that case, so the runner never starts.
#
# Merging: tool PRs are NOT merged by this workflow. The seo-tool-validate
# workflow smoke-tests the built tool live and labels it tool-validated; the
# auto-merge gate only merges tool PRs carrying that label.

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [seo-tool-approved]
  schedule:
    - cron: "42 19 * * 3" # Wednesdays 19:42 UTC - dead-man's switch only, see above
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: seo-tool-build
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # continue-on-error at JOB level: a failure still runs the failure() steps
    # and still reports to the dashboard rails, but the RUN concludes green so
    # GitHub never emails the repo owner "Run failed". The dashboard Home
    # banner / get_cron_health are the alerting surface for these runs.
    continue-on-error: true
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read # the outcome report reads which step failed
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The agent commits below. Pin an identity that maps to a real GitHub
      # account - Vercel refuses to deploy commits from unknown author emails,
      # and an unconfigured runner leaves the agent to improvise one.
      - name: Pin git identity to github-actions[bot]
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Skip if a tool PR is already open or tool builds are toggled off
        id: guard
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          open=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --label seo-tool --state open --json number --jq 'length')
          if [ "$open" != "0" ]; then
            echo "A tool PR is already open - skipping. The suggestion stays approved; the weekly sweep will pick it up once the open PR lands."
            echo "skip_reason=a tool PR is already open and unmerged" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Automation-flag gate: the DispatchSEO dashboard can pause tool
          # builds (auto_build_tools off). 404 = backend without the endpoint
          # yet -> build as before; other failures are loud.
          if [ "$open" = "0" ]; then
            code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/mode.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
            if [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.automations.auto_build_tools' /tmp/mode.json)" = "false" ]; then
              echo "Tool builds are toggled off on the dashboard - skipping. The suggestion stays approved."
              open=paused
            elif [ "$code" = "unreachable" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ] || [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "503" ] || [ "$code" = "504" ]; then
              # Self-hosted backends reboot (kernel updates, docker restarts).
              # Unreachable is a delay, not a failure - the later scheduled
              # attempt and the in-stack builder both cover this window.
              echo "Backend unreachable right now (rebooting?) - deferring to the next scheduled attempt."
              open=defer
              echo "skip_reason=the backend was unreachable, so this run was deferred" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            elif [ "$code" != "200" ] && [ "$code" != "404" ]; then
              echo "::error::project-mode endpoint returned HTTP $code"; exit 1
            fi
          fi
          # Already-ran-today gate, for the dead-man's cron: it must not redo
          # work an earlier dispatch already did the same day. Reuses the
          # project-mode fetch above (same tolerant rule: anything but a clean
          # "true" reads as "not run yet").
          # SCHEDULE-only. This exists so the fallback does not redo the
          # dispatched run's work; it was never meant to gate an ON-DEMAND run.
          # Without the event_name test, an owner approving a tool after that
          # day's sweep had the build silently skipped - every step no-op'd, the
          # final step still reported ok=1, and the next chance was seven days
          # later (2026-07-27).
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ] && [ "$open" = "0" ] && [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.ran_today."seo-tools" // false' /tmp/mode.json 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]; then
            echo "Today's tool sweep already ran - skipping this attempt."
            open=skip
          fi
          # Empty-queue gate. The backend never dispatches with nothing
          # approved, so this is for the dead-man's cron: without it, a weekly
          # fallback on a project with an empty tool queue starts a full
          # coding-agent session purely to have the agent exit clean.
          # Absent field (older backend) or any non-200 reads as "work is
          # waiting", so this can only ever cost a run, never suppress one.
          if [ "$open" = "0" ] && [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.approved_waiting.tool // true' /tmp/mode.json 2>/dev/null)" = "false" ]; then
            echo "No approved tool suggestions are waiting - nothing to build."
            open=skip
          fi
          echo "open=$open" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # >>> agent-steps: resolve (GENERATED - edit scripts/agent-ci/ and regenerate; never edit between these markers)
      # Which coding agent runs this workflow - resolved at RUN time from the
      # dashboard, never baked in at install time. A decision left to whoever
      # ran the install is a decision someone eventually forgets, and the
      # failure mode here is a builder that runs the wrong agent every night.
      # Asking the backend means switching agent on the dashboard takes effect
      # on the next scheduled run with nothing to edit in this repo.
      #
      # The fallback matters as much as the happy path: a repo installed against
      # a backend that predates the `agent` field gets no value here, and must
      # keep behaving exactly as it did - which is claude, because Claude was
      # the only option that ever existed before the field.
      - name: Resolve the coding agent
        id: agent
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          CLAUDE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          agent=""
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/agent.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
          [ "$code" = "200" ] && agent=$(jq -r '.agent // empty' /tmp/agent.json 2>/dev/null)
          if [ -z "$agent" ] || [ "$agent" = "null" ]; then
            # No answer from the backend. Infer from which secret exists, and
            # tie-break to claude - see the note above.
            if [ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ] && [ -z "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then agent=codex
            elif [ -n "$CURSOR_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ] && [ -z "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then agent=cursor
            else agent=claude
            fi
            echo "Backend did not name an agent (HTTP $code) - inferred '$agent' from the secrets on this repo."
          fi
          # Fail here, in plain language, rather than letting the agent's own
          # action die minutes in on a cryptic validation error. The 2026-07-17
          # dogfood install burned four runs on exactly that.
          case "$agent" in
            claude)
              if [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ] && [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "No CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN on this repo - running Claude on the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret instead (metered API billing on your Anthropic account)."
              elif [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Claude Code, but the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret is missing or empty on this repo (and there is no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret to fall back on). Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard (it mints and VERIFIES a fresh token), or set one by hand: run 'claude setup-token', then pipe the token into 'gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN' without any whitespace. Or run on metered API billing instead: create a key at console.anthropic.com and pipe it into 'gh secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'."
                exit 1
              else
                case "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" in
                  sk-ant-oat*) : ;;
                  *)
                    echo "::error::CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN does not look like a Claude Code OAuth token (expected it to start with sk-ant-oat). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to mint and verify a replacement."
                    exit 1 ;;
                esac
                if [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then
                  echo "Both CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are set - the subscription token takes precedence. To run on the API key instead: gh secret delete CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN."
                fi
              fi ;;
            codex)
              if [ -z "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Codex, but the OPENAI_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. Add it with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY', or rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$OPENAI_API_KEY" in
                sk-*) : ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::OPENAI_API_KEY does not look like an OpenAI key (expected it to start with sk-). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Create a fresh key at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again."
                  exit 1 ;;
              esac ;;
            cursor)
              if [ -z "$CURSOR_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Cursor, but the CURSOR_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. A runner has no browser, so the interactive 'cursor-agent login' is not an option here - only an API key works. Mint one at cursor.com/dashboard/api (open the URL directly; any plan can) and add it with 'gh secret set CURSOR_API_KEY', or switch this project to Claude Code or Codex on your DispatchSEO dashboard."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$CURSOR_API_KEY" in
                sk-ant-*)
                  echo "::error::CURSOR_API_KEY holds a Claude credential (it starts with sk-ant-). The wrong secret was pasted. Put the Claude token in CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and a Cursor API key here."
                  exit 1 ;;
                sk-*)
                  echo "::error::CURSOR_API_KEY holds an OpenAI key (it starts with sk-). The wrong secret was pasted. Put the OpenAI key in OPENAI_API_KEY and a Cursor API key here."
                  exit 1 ;;
                *[[:space:]]*)
                  # [[:space:]], never a literal tab in the pattern: a tab
                  # character in generated YAML is invalid indentation, and
                  # pipeline-pack-lint fails the build on it.
                  echo "::error::CURSOR_API_KEY contains whitespace, which almost always means it was line-wrapped when it was copied. Re-copy the key and set it again with: printf '%s' \"\$KEY\" | tr -d '[:space:]' | gh secret set CURSOR_API_KEY"
                  exit 1 ;;
                *) : ;;
              esac ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::The dashboard reported an unknown agent '$agent'. This repo's workflows are older than that setting - re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to update them."
              exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "agent=$agent" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Building with: $agent"
      # <<< agent-steps: resolve


      # Fail loudly if the seo-manager MCP is unreachable. Without this, a
      # stale URL in mcp-ci.json makes Claude see an empty toolset and "exit
      # cleanly" - a green run that built nothing (2026-07-14 domain-move bug).
      - name: Preflight - seo-manager MCP reachable
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          url=$(node -e "console.log(require('./.github/mcp-ci.json').mcpServers['seo-manager'].url)")
          code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 -X POST "$url" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
            -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"tools/list"}')
          if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::seo-manager MCP at $url returned HTTP $code - fix the URL in .github/mcp-ci.json or the SEO_MCP_API_KEY secret"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "seo-manager MCP OK ($url)"

      # Deliberately NOT an INSTALL-ADAPT step. Which package manager this
      # repo uses is resolved at RUN time - packageManager pin first, then
      # lockfiles - never by an install-time edit, because an edit whose
      # omission is fatal is banned (scripts/pipeline-pack-lint.mjs; the
      # 2026-07-30 incident where a missed DELETE-this-line killed every
      # pinned repo's builder at step 2 is why). Assuming every repo is pnpm
      # was the same bug one layer up: the zero-touch cloud install commits
      # this pack verbatim into repos nobody adapted, and the first real
      # cloud customer's npm+Vite site died 25 seconds into every build
      # (2026-08-02). pnpm keeps its two blessed shapes (pinned reads the
      # pin, unpinned pins the action - a version input on a step that also
      # sees a packageManager pin is what hard-errors); npm/yarn/bun get
      # their own installs; no package.json at all skips Node setup entirely
      # and the agent works from the repo's real build story in
      # .dispatchseo/conventions.md.
      - name: Detect this repo's package manager
        id: pkg
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        run: |
          pm=none; pnpm_pinned=0; cache=""
          if [ -f package.json ]; then
            field=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(String(require("./package.json").packageManager || ""))' 2>/dev/null || true)
            case "$field" in
              pnpm@*) pm=pnpm; pnpm_pinned=1 ;;
              yarn@*) pm=yarn ;;
              npm@*)  pm=npm ;;
              bun@*)  pm=bun ;;
            esac
            if [ "$pm" = "none" ]; then
              if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then pm=pnpm
              elif [ -f package-lock.json ]; then pm=npm
              elif [ -f yarn.lock ]; then pm=yarn
              elif [ -f bun.lock ] || [ -f bun.lockb ]; then pm=bun
              else pm=npm
              fi
            fi
          fi
          # setup-node's cache input hard-errors when the matching lockfile is
          # missing, so only request a cache that provably exists.
          case "$pm" in
            pnpm) if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then cache=pnpm; fi ;;
            npm)  if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then cache=npm; fi ;;
            yarn) if [ -f yarn.lock ]; then cache=yarn; fi ;;
          esac
          # Node major, resolved at RUN time - same rule and same reason as the
          # package manager above. `node-version: 22` was hardcoded here while
          # the install playbook told the installing agent to hand-edit it if
          # the repo built on something else, which is the banned shape exactly:
          # a pack update pushes this file VERBATIM, so that edit self-reverts
          # on the next sync and the builder then dies on the wrong major in a
          # repo nobody is watching (2026-08-02).
          #
          # .nvmrc first - a repo that ships one has DECLARED the version its
          # own developers build on, so it is honoured as written. engines.node
          # is read as a FLOOR rather than a target: ">=18" is a minimum a Node
          # 22 runner already satisfies, and resolving it downward would move
          # working installs onto an EOL major - and below pnpm 11's own floor -
          # to satisfy a constraint that was never violated. 22 when neither
          # file says anything, which is what every install already runs, so a
          # repo that declares nothing sees no change at all.
          node_v=22
          if [ -f .nvmrc ]; then
            # Tolerates "v22", "22.11.0" and trailing whitespace; an alias like
            # "lts/*" names no number, so the default stands.
            v=$(grep -Eo '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+){0,2}' .nvmrc 2>/dev/null | head -1)
            [ -n "$v" ] && node_v="$v"
          elif [ -f package.json ]; then
            eng=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(String((require("./package.json").engines||{}).node||""))' 2>/dev/null || true)
            major=$(printf '%s' "$eng" | grep -Eo '[0-9]+' | head -1)
            if [ -n "$major" ] && [ "$major" -gt 22 ]; then node_v="$major"; fi
          fi
          { echo "pm=$pm"; echo "pnpm_pinned=$pnpm_pinned"; echo "cache=$cache"; echo "node=$node_v"; } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "package manager: $pm (pnpm pin: $pnpm_pinned, node cache: ${cache:-off}, node: $node_v)"

      # Pinned -> action-setup reads the exact version out of the field.
      # Passing a version input as well is precisely what hard-errors.
      - name: Set up pnpm (version from the repo's packageManager pin)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pkg.outputs.pm == 'pnpm' && steps.pkg.outputs.pnpm_pinned == '1'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4

      # No pin -> action-setup has to be told. pnpm 11 matches the Node 22
      # floor resolved above; a repo whose lockfile was written by an older
      # major should add a packageManager field rather than edit this, which
      # routes it to the exact path above.
      - name: Set up pnpm (no packageManager pin in this repo)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pkg.outputs.pm == 'pnpm' && steps.pkg.outputs.pnpm_pinned == '0'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4
        with:
          version: 11

      - name: Set up Bun
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pkg.outputs.pm == 'bun'
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2

      - name: Set up Node
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pkg.outputs.pm != 'none'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          # Resolved by the detection step above, never hand-edited - see the
